BALA.phala: In the Infant (Bala) state a planet gives only a quarter (25%) of its result.
BALA.phalaProse: A planet occupying the first 6 degrees of an odd sign or the last 6 degrees of an even sign is in the Bala (infant) avastha. Akin to a newborn, it is weak and cannot express its full potency, yielding only about a quarter (25%) of its promised effects. These results gradually mature and strengthen in the later phases of life.

KUMARA.phala: In the Adolescent (Kumara) state a planet gives half (50%) of its result.
KUMARA.phalaProse: A planet occupying 6 to 12 degrees of an odd sign or 18 to 24 degrees of an even sign is in the Kumara (adolescent) avastha. Having grew past infancy but not yet fully matured, it possesses half-strength and delivers 50% of its potential results, which steadily expand as the native matures.

MRITA.phala: In the Dead (Mrita) state a planet is devoid of strength and virtually inactive.
MRITA.phalaProse: A planet positioned in the last 6 degrees of an odd sign (24 to 30 degrees) or the first 6 degrees of an even sign (0 to 6 degrees) is in the Mrita (dead) avastha. Deprived of vital energy, it is rendered virtually inactive, producing next to no positive or noticeable effects for its houses and indications.

VRIDDHA.phala: In the Old (Vriddha) state a planet’s strength declines, giving diminished results.
VRIDDHA.phalaProse: A planet occupying 18 to 24 degrees of an odd sign or 6 to 12 degrees of an even sign is in the Vriddha (old) avastha. Like a person in advanced age, its energy is declining, resulting in significantly diminished and weakened expression of its significations.

YUVA.phala: In the Youthful (Yuva) state a planet gives its full result (100%).
YUVA.phalaProse: A planet positioned between 12 and 18 degrees in either an odd or even sign is in the Yuva (youthful) avastha. Endowed with the peak vitality of youth, it functions at maximum capacity and delivers 100% of its natural and structural results. This represents the absolute pinnacle of planetary strength in this division.

DEEPTA.phala: Exalted in the radiant (Deepta) state, the planet amplifies worldly success, eminence, and fortune.
DEEPTA.phalaProse: When a planet occupies its sign of highest exaltation, it enters the Deepta (radiant) avastha. Blazing with exceptional strength, it increases public recognition, substantial wealth, and robust physical health. The planet's natural and house-based significations manifest at their absolute peak of auspiciousness.

DINA.phala: In the Dina (miserable) state a planet, in an enemy sign, gives depleted and stressful results.
DINA.phalaProse: A planet positioned in an enemy's sign is in the Dina (miserable, depleted) avastha. Operating in a hostile environment, it loses its operational capacity, leading to persistent self-doubt, struggles with authority, financial constraints, and general lack of fulfillment in its domains.

DUKHI.phala: In the Dukhi (sorrowful) state a planet, joined with a malefic or enemy, gives painful results.
DUKHI.phalaProse: A planet conjoined with a malefic or an enemy planet is in the Dukhi (sorrowful) avastha. Burdened by malefic friction, it brings mental anxiety, structural delays, and domestic friction. The house it rules becomes a source of emotional challenge and strain.

KHALA.phala: In the Khala (wicked) state a planet, debilitated, yields harsh and difficult challenges.
KHALA.phalaProse: A planet placed in its sign of debilitation is in the Khala (wicked, low-functioning) avastha. Devoid of structural dignity, it can provoke lapses in judgment, internal frustration, friction with society, and material depletion, unless rescued by strong cancellation (Neecha-bhanga).

KOPA.phala: In the Kopa (angry) state a planet, defeated in war or afflicted, yields volatile and harsh outcomes.
KOPA.phalaProse: A planet defeated in planetary war (graha yuddha) or heavily afflicted by harsh aspects is in the Kopa (angry) avastha. Behaving erratically due to distress, it introduces sudden outbursts of anger, litigation, and aggressive confrontations, causing stress in the areas of life it governs.

MUDITA.phala: In the Mudita (delighted) state a planet, in a friend’s sign, yields happy and cooperative results.
MUDITA.phalaProse: A planet in a friendly sign is in the Mudita (delighted) avastha. Experiencing harmony and welcome, it fosters cooperative relationships, learning, financial gains, and genuine mental happiness. It naturally attracts supportive opportunities and friendships.

SHANTA.phala: In the Shanta (peaceful) state a planet, in a benefic varga, brings calm and spiritual growth.
SHANTA.phalaProse: A planet occupying benefic divisions (vargas) or influenced by benefic aspects is in the Shanta (peaceful) avastha. Reflecting a calm, quiet strength, it channels the mind toward ethical behavior, inner peace, and intellectual discrimination, yielding serene and auspicious outcomes.

SWASTHA.phala: In the Swastha (healthy) state a planet, in its own sign, gives stable and nourishing results.
SWASTHA.phalaProse: A planet placed in its own sign is in the Swastha (healthy, at-ease) avastha. Comfortable and secure in its own domain, it bestows physical health, internal contentment, and structural stability. Its effects are durable, dependable, and highly constructive.

VIKALA.phala: In the Vikala (crippled) state a combust planet has its significations eclipsed and weakened.
VIKALA.phalaProse: A planet combust due to its extreme proximity to the Sun is in the Vikala (crippled, combust) avastha. Having its light and independence eclipsed by solar glare, it struggling to deliver its results, which are often distorted or felt as internal cravings rather than external realities.

JAGRAT.phala: In the Waking (Jagrat) state a planet is fully alert and gives full results.
JAGRAT.phalaProse: A planet placed in its sign of exaltation or its own sign is in the Jagrat (waking) avastha. Being fully alert and conscious, it expresses the results of its natural and structural significations with maximum clarity, vigor, and success.

SUSHUPTI.phala: In the Sleeping (Sushupti) state a planet gives weak, dormant results.
SUSHUPTI.phalaProse: A planet placed in an enemy sign or its sign of debilitation is in the Sushupti (deep sleep) avastha. Operating as if in deep, unconscious slumber, its energy is entirely dormant, rendering its significations weak, inactive, or highly blocked.

SWAPNA.phala: In the Dreaming (Swapna) state a planet gives moderate, mixed results.
SWAPNA.phalaProse: A planet in a friendly or neutral sign is in the Swapna (dreaming) avastha. Behaving as if in a semi-conscious or dreaming state, it gives moderate, mixed, or partially expressed results — neither functioning at full strength nor completely failing.

GARVITA.phala: In the Garvita (proud) state an exalted or mooltrikona planet confers power, wealth, and authority.
GARVITA.phalaProse: A planet placed in its exaltation or moolatrikona sign is in the Garvita (proud, majestic) avastha. Filled with structural dignity and pride, it bestows eminent public positions, administrative authority, financial prosperity, and an unshakeable sense of self-belief.

KSHOBHITA.phala: In the Kshobhita (agitated) state a planet, scorched and afflicted, induces blockages and mental anxiety.
KSHOBHITA.phalaProse: A planet conjoined with the Sun and simultaneously aspected by a malefic enters the Kshobhita (agitated) avastha. Heavily stressed by both solar combustion and malefic friction, it creates extreme restlessness, sudden delays in enterprises, and friction in communication, causing major stress in its operational houses.

KSHUDHA.phala: In the Kshudha (hungry) state a planet, afflicted by enemies, brings material struggle and chronic dissatisfaction.
KSHUDHA.phalaProse: A planet placed in an enemy's sign or in close contact with enemy planets enters the Kshudha (hungry) avastha. Starved of protective dignity, it acts as a vacuum in the chart, creating persistent material wants, delays in career advancement, and a chronic sense of emotional or financial dissatisfaction.

LAJJITA.phala: In the Lajjita (ashamed) state a planet, shamed in the 5th, delays progeny and clouds intellect.
LAJJITA.phalaProse: A planet located in the 5th house in conjunction with Rahu, Ketu, Sun, Saturn, or Mars enters the Lajjita (ashamed) avastha. Feeling restricted and shamed in this key house of intellect and creation, it generates self-doubt, delays or challenges in childbearing, and difficulties in creative expression.

MUDITA.phala: In the Mudita (delighted) state a planet, supported by benefics and friends, yields smooth prosperity.
MUDITA.phalaProse: A planet in a friendly sign or conjoined with benefic planets is in the Mudita (delighted) avastha. Highly comfortable, it acts as a magnet for constructive growth, bringing warm familial bonds, financial abundance, and a general ease in overcoming obstacles.

TRISHITA.phala: In the Trishita (thirsty) state a planet, watery and afflicted, provokes emotional instability and cravings.
TRISHITA.phalaProse: A planet situated in a watery sign and aspected or joined by a malefic is in the Trishita (thirsty) avastha. Driven by unquenchable desire, it triggers emotional instability, excessive cravings, restlessness, and feelings of vulnerability in relationships and mental peace.

JUPITER.colourProse: Jupiter’s auspicious colours are yellow and gold; these strengthen wisdom, dharma and prosperity.
JUPITER.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Jupiter period.
JUPITER.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Jupiter, this yoga gives its results — in the form of wisdom, wealth, dharma and progeny.
JUPITER.dashaPhala: The Jupiter dasha brings wisdom, wealth, progeny and dharma; when weak, loss of faith and disorders of fat and liver.
JUPITER.dashaPhalaProse: Jupiter's Mahadasha lasts sixteen years. A strong, benefic Jupiter grants wisdom, abundance of wealth and grain, the happiness of children, devotion to dharma, honour from teachers, the divine and the learned, promotion and fame; the native becomes virtuous, generous, discerning and devout. An afflicted or weak Jupiter can bring loss of faith, distress through children, obesity, liver ailments, irreligion and financial loss. As the significator of wisdom, wealth and progeny and the planet of ether, Jupiter's period is auspicious and expansive.
JUPITER.directionProse: The favourable direction of Jupiter is the Northeast; facing it for work grants wisdom, dharma and prosperity.
JUPITER.mantra: Chant the Jupiter mantra in the morning, facing Northeast.
JUPITER.mantraProse: The Jupiter mantra is best chanted in the morning facing northeast, on a Thursday, with yellow flowers and sandal.

KETU.colourProse: Ketu’s auspicious colours are smoky and brownish; these strengthen detachment, liberation and spirituality.
KETU.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Ketu period.
KETU.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Ketu, this yoga gives its results — in the form of detachment, liberation, spirituality and occult knowledge.
KETU.dashaPhala: The Ketu dasha brings detachment, a turn toward liberation and spiritual attainment; when afflicted, distress, fear and obscure ailments.
KETU.dashaPhalaProse: Ketu's Mahadasha lasts seven years. A well-placed or strong Ketu grants spiritual advancement, the wisdom of detachment, an inclination toward liberation, mastery of occult knowledge, pilgrimage and unexpected gains; the native becomes introspective, discerning and seeking of moksha. An afflicted or weak Ketu can bring causeless distress, vague fear, obscure ailments that defy diagnosis, calumny, separation from kin and mental disturbance. As a shadowy planet and the significator of liberation, Ketu's period is a time of detachment and inner discipline.
KETU.direction: Ketu’s direction is the Southwest (and South).
KETU.directionProse: The favourable direction of Ketu is the Southwest; facing it for work grants detachment, liberation and spiritual attainment.
KETU.mantra: Chant the Ketu mantra in the evening, facing Southwest.
KETU.mantraProse: The Ketu mantra is best chanted in the evening facing southwest, on a Tuesday, with brownish offerings.

MARS.colourProse: Mars’s auspicious colours are red and crimson; these strengthen prowess, courage and zeal.
MARS.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Mars period.
MARS.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Mars, this yoga gives its results — in the form of valour, courage and matters of land.
MARS.dashaPhala: The Mars dasha brings valour, gain of land and courage; when afflicted, blood disorders, strife and wounds.
MARS.dashaPhalaProse: Mars's Mahadasha lasts seven years. A strong, benefic Mars grants prowess, acquisition of land, the welfare of brothers, martial success, victory over enemies, courage and success in enterprise; the native is energetic, fearless and active. An afflicted or weak Mars can bring disorders of blood and bile, wounds, danger from fire and weapons, quarrels, distress to brothers and high blood pressure. As the fiery significator of valour (Parakrama), the Mars period is a time of courage and conflict.
MARS.directionProse: The favourable direction of Mars is the South; facing south for work grants prowess and courage.
MARS.mantra: Chant the Mars mantra in the morning, facing South.
MARS.mantraProse: The Mars mantra is best chanted in the morning facing south, on a Tuesday, with red flowers and jaggery.

MERCURY.colourProse: Mercury’s auspicious colour is green; it strengthens intellect, learning, communication and trade.
MERCURY.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Mercury period.
MERCURY.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Mercury, this yoga gives its results — in the form of intellect, speech and trade.
MERCURY.dashaPhala: The Mercury dasha brings learning, commercial skill and wealth; when afflicted, speech troubles, skin ailments and confusion.
MERCURY.dashaPhalaProse: Mercury's Mahadasha lasts seventeen years. A strong, benefic Mercury grants learning, success in trade, intellectual brilliance, skill in writing and speech, the happiness of friends, gain of wealth and proficiency in mathematics; the native is clever, eloquent and adept in dealings. An afflicted or weak Mercury can bring troubles of speech, skin ailments, nervous weakness, mental confusion, loss in business and calumny. As the significator of intellect and speech and the earthy planet, Mercury's period governs learning and commerce.
MERCURY.directionProse: The favourable direction of Mercury is the North; facing north for work grants intellect, learning and trade.
MERCURY.mantra: Chant the Mercury mantra in the morning, facing North.
MERCURY.mantraProse: The Mercury mantra is best chanted in the morning facing north, on a Wednesday, with green flowers.

MOON.colourProse: The Moon’s auspicious colours are white and silver; these strengthen peace of mind, gentleness and maternal comfort.
MOON.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Moon period.
MOON.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of the Moon, this yoga gives its results — in the form of mental comfort and matters of the mother.
MOON.dashaPhala: The Moon dasha brings peace of mind, motherly comfort and wealth; when weak, mental distress and phlegmatic ailments.
MOON.dashaPhalaProse: The Moon's Mahadasha lasts ten years. A strong, benefic Moon grants peace of mind, the comfort of the mother, gain of wealth, travel by water, prosperity, popularity and the happiness of women; the native is gentle, emotional and imaginative. A waning or afflicted Moon can bring mental restlessness, melancholy, phlegmatic fevers, distress to the mother, loss of wealth and insomnia. As the watery Manahkaraka (significator of the mind), the Moon's period chiefly governs the emotions and relationships.
MOON.direction: The Moon’s direction is the Northwest.
MOON.directionProse: The favourable direction of the Moon is the Northwest; facing it for work grants peace of mind and maternal comfort.
MOON.mantra: Chant the Moon mantra at night, facing Northwest.
MOON.mantraProse: The Moon mantra is best chanted at night facing northwest, on a Monday, with white flowers and water.

RAHU.colourProse: Rahu’s auspicious colours are smoky grey and blue-tinged; these strengthen sudden gains, insight and daring.
RAHU.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Rahu period.
RAHU.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Rahu, this yoga gives its results — in the form of sudden gains, foreign connections and ambition.
RAHU.dashaPhala: The Rahu dasha brings sudden gains, foreign connections and ambition; when afflicted, confusion, fear and toxic ailments.
RAHU.dashaPhalaProse: Rahu's Mahadasha lasts eighteen years. A well-placed or strong Rahu grants sudden gains of wealth, foreign travel, political rise, unconventional success, fame and achievement in extraordinary undertakings; the native becomes ambitious, diplomatic and unorthodox. An afflicted or weak Rahu can bring mental confusion, baseless fear, ailments from poisons and infection, calumny, deception, mental unrest and sudden loss. As a shadowy planet and the significator of illusion (Maya), Rahu's period yields uncertain results and drives intense change.
RAHU.directionProse: The favourable direction of Rahu is the Southwest; facing it for work grants sudden success and foreign connections.
RAHU.mantra: Chant the Rahu mantra in the evening, facing Southwest.
RAHU.mantraProse: The Rahu mantra is best chanted in the evening facing southwest, on a Saturday, with smoky offerings.

SATURN.colourProse: Saturn’s auspicious colours are dark blue and black; these strengthen patience, work, stability and justice.
SATURN.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Saturn period.
SATURN.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Saturn, this yoga gives its results — in the form of work, patience, service and long-term gains (slowly, but lastingly).
SATURN.dashaPhala: The Saturn dasha brings toil, delay, detachment and the fruit of karma; when afflicted, sorrow, disease and poverty.
SATURN.dashaPhalaProse: Saturn's Mahadasha lasts nineteen years. A strong, benefic Saturn grants lasting accomplishment through patience and labour, a position of service, the support of land and the masses, long-term gains, and the discernment of detachment; the native becomes industrious, enduring and just. An afflicted or weak Saturn can bring sorrow, delay, disorders of wind (rheumatic and nervous), poverty, loss of position, depression and separation from kin. As the airy significator of karma and longevity, Saturn's period is a time of toil, testing and maturation.
SATURN.directionProse: The favourable direction of Saturn is the West; facing west for work grants patience, work and stability.
SATURN.mantra: Chant the Saturn mantra in the evening, facing West.
SATURN.mantraProse: The Saturn mantra is best chanted in the evening facing west, on a Saturday, with blue flowers and oil.

SUN.colour: The Sun’s colour is red / copper.
SUN.colourProse: The Sun’s auspicious colours are red, copper and saffron; these strengthen self-confidence, vigour and standing.
SUN.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Sun period.
SUN.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of the Sun, this yoga gives its results — in the form of standing, authority and vitality.
SUN.dashaPhala: The Sun dasha brings authority, vitality and recognition, but can bring bilious ailments and conflict with superiors.
SUN.dashaPhalaProse: The Sun's Mahadasha lasts six years. When the Sun is strong and well-placed it grants royal favour, authority, the well-being of the father, good health, elevation in position, and courage; the native becomes radiant, self-assured and capable of leadership. When the Sun is weak or afflicted by malefics it can bring bilious fevers, eye ailments, distress to the father, friction with those in power, and loss of position. As the fiery Atmakaraka, the Sun's period is fundamentally a time of self-assertion, fame and standing.
SUN.direction: The Sun’s direction is the East.
SUN.directionProse: The favourable direction of the Sun is the East; facing east for work and worship grants vigour and strength.
SUN.mantra: Chant the Sun mantra at sunrise, facing East.
SUN.mantraProse: The Sun mantra is best chanted at sunrise facing east, on a Sunday, with an offering of water from a copper vessel.

VENUS.colourProse: Venus’s auspicious colours are white, pink and variegated; these strengthen comfort, fortune, art and marital happiness.
VENUS.dashaActivation: The yoga’s results ripen in a Venus period.
VENUS.dashaActivationProse: In the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Venus, this yoga gives its results — in the form of comfort, luxury, marriage and art.
VENUS.dashaPhala: The Venus dasha brings comfort, luxury, artistic fortune and marital happiness; when afflicted, desire-borne troubles and urinary ailments.
VENUS.dashaPhalaProse: Venus's Mahadasha lasts twenty years. A strong, benefic Venus grants comfort and prosperity, the gain of vehicles, ornaments and fine garments, love of art and music, marital happiness, the good fortune of women and a life of enjoyment and affluence; the native is fond of beauty, refined and attractive. An afflicted or weak Venus can bring troubles born of desire, marital discord, disorders of the urinary and reproductive organs, diabetes and loss through over-indulgence. As the watery significator of art, desire and enjoyment, Venus's period is a time of comfort, fortune and pleasure.
VENUS.directionProse: The favourable direction of Venus is the Southeast; facing it for work grants comfort, fortune and marital happiness.
VENUS.mantra: Chant the Venus mantra in the morning, facing Southeast.
VENUS.mantraProse: The Venus mantra is best chanted in the morning facing southeast, on a Friday, with white flowers and fragrance.

ABHUKTA_MOOLA_DOSHA.timing: Abhukta-Moola Dosha signals junction-born effects in early childhood.
ABHUKTA_MOOLA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Abhukta-Moola Dosha (birth at the junction of the end of Jyeshtha and the start of Mula) fructifies chiefly in the first years of childhood. The window can bring distress to the child’s health and indications of risk near the parents. Special care is advised at the start of the Ashtottari dasha; propitiation (Mula shanti) removes it.

AMAVASYA_DOSHA.timing: Amavasya Dosha signals loss of mental strength during a Moon dasha and weak Moon transits.
AMAVASYA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Amavasya Dosha (birth with a waning Moon near the new Moon) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of the Moon and during transits near the new Moon. The window can bring loss of mental strength, low self-confidence, obstacles to the comfort of the mother, and melancholy. Benefic associations and the full-Moon transit ease it.

ANGARAK_DOSHA.timing: Angarak Dosha (Mars–Rahu) signals anger, fire and accidents during a Mars or Rahu dasha.
ANGARAK_DOSHA.timingProse: The Angarak Dosha (Mars conjoined with Rahu) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Mars and Rahu. The window can bring excessive anger, disorders of blood and bile, danger of accidents from fire and weapons, and sudden quarrels. Mars transiting the natal Rahu position sharpens it; patience and restraint ease it.

ANSHIK_MANGAL.timing: Anshik (partial) Mangal Dosha signals mild marital friction during a Mars dasha and marriage.
ANSHIK_MANGAL.timingProse: The Anshik (partial) Mangal Dosha — a lighter degree of Kuja affliction — fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Mars and around marriageable age. Compared with full Mangal Dosha the distress is slighter: minor marital disagreement or initial delay. Mars transiting the 7th sharpens it; where a cancellation applies it is usually negligible.

BADHAKA_DOSHA.timing: Badhaka Dosha signals obstruction during the dasha of the Badhaka lord and its transits.
BADHAKA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Badhaka Dosha fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of the Badhaka lord (the 11th lord for movable signs, the 9th for fixed, the 7th for dual). The window can bring sudden obstacles, delay in work, hidden opposition, and hindrance just as success approaches. The Badhaka lord transiting the Badhaka house sharpens it; propitiation of the Badhaka lord eases it.

BANDHU_DOSHA.timing: Bandhu Dosha signals obstacles to home and mother during the 4th-lord dasha.
BANDHU_DOSHA.timingProse: The Bandhu Dosha fructifies during the dasha of the 4th lord (lord of home and kin) and grahas connected to it. The window can bring obstacles to the comfort of the mother, domestic discord, friction with relatives, and hindrance in immovable property. Kantaka Shani (Saturn transiting the 4th) sharpens it; a strong 4th lord eases it.

BHADRA_DOSHA.timing: Bhadra Dosha (Vishti karana birth) signals obstruction in undertakings tied to that karana.
BHADRA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Bhadra Dosha (birth in the Vishti/Bhadra karana) fructifies at the start of auspicious undertakings and during the transit of the Bhadra karana. The window can bring obstruction to auspicious work, delay at the outset, and sudden hindrance. Avoiding the "face" of Bhadra and choosing an auspicious muhurta removes it.

BHAKOOT_DOSHA.timing: Bhakoot Dosha signals marital disharmony in married life and adverse Moon-sign transits.
BHAKOOT_DOSHA.timingProse: The Bhakoot Dosha (an adverse 6–8 or 2–12 relation between the partners’ Moon signs) fructifies after marriage, within married life. The window can bring a lack of mental union, disparity in finances and progeny, and mutual disagreement. Friendship between the sign lords and planetary strength ease it; adverse transit positions of the two Moons sharpen it.

BRAHMA_DOSHA.timing: Brahma Dosha signals results of lapsed family dharma during a Jupiter or 2nd/5th-lord dasha.
BRAHMA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Brahma Dosha (indicating ancestral lapses of dharma) tends to act during the Mahadasha of Jupiter, the significator of dharma, and in periods of the 2nd, 5th and 9th lords. This window can bring distress born of neglected family observance, obstacles to progeny, and interruption to education. A benefic Jupiter transit through the 5th or 9th eases it; worship and charity to the learned bring relief.

CHANDAL_DOSHA.timing: Chandal Dosha (Jupiter–Rahu) signals confusion of dharma and judgement during a Jupiter–Rahu dasha.
CHANDAL_DOSHA.timingProse: The Chandal Dosha (Jupiter conjoined with Rahu, akin to Guru-Chandal) fructifies during the dasha of Jupiter and Rahu. The window can bring confusion of dharma and judgement, friction with teachers, attraction to unethical ways, and hindrance in higher education. A benefic Jupiter transit through its own, exaltation or a friendly sign eases it.

CHANDRA_DOSHA.timing: Chandra Dosha signals mental and maternal distress during a Moon dasha and weak Moon transits.
CHANDRA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Chandra Dosha (affliction of the Moon) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of the Moon, and during transits of a waning Moon near the new Moon. The window can bring mental restlessness, melancholy, distress to the mother, phlegmatic ailments and broken sleep. A benefic Moon transit and the period near the full Moon ease it.

DAGDHA_RASHI_DOSHA.timing: Dagdha-Rashi Dosha signals loss of that house’s results during the dasha of its lord.
DAGDHA_RASHI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Dagdha-Rashi Dosha (a planet placed in a sign "burnt" by the weekday–tithi combination) fructifies during the dasha of the burnt sign’s lord and the planets within it. The window can bring loss of the results of the related house, fruitless effort, and mixed outcomes. A benefic aspect and strength somewhat improve the result.

DARIDRA_DOSHA.timing: Daridra Dosha signals financial strain and excess expenditure during the 2nd/11th-lord dasha.
DARIDRA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Daridra Dosha (affliction of the houses of wealth and gain) fructifies during the dasha of the 2nd lord, the 11th lord, and the grahas that afflict them. The window can bring financial strain, excessive expenditure, mounting debt and obstacles to savings. A benefic dasha or transit through the 2nd or 11th eases it.

ECLIPSE_DOSHA.timing: Eclipse-birth Dosha signals intense effects during the dasha of luminaries/nodes and eclipses.
ECLIPSE_DOSHA.timingProse: The Eclipse-birth Dosha (birth during an eclipse) fructifies during the dasha of the Sun, Moon, Rahu and Ketu, and during actual eclipses. The window can bring distress to health, mental unrest, obstacles to the welfare of the parents, and sudden hindrance. Eclipse propitiation, japa and charity remove it.

GANA_DOSHA.timing: Gana Dosha signals distress through temperamental mismatch after marriage.
GANA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Gana Dosha (a mismatch of Deva/Manushya/Rakshasa temperament between partners, especially a Deva–Rakshasa pairing) fructifies after marriage. The window can bring difference of nature, mental disagreement and mutual discontent. Friendship between the sign lords and a difference of Nadi ease it; a strong Moon brings mental union.

GANDANTA_DOSHA.timing: Gandanta Dosha signals risk in early childhood and at the junction nakshatra/sign transits.
GANDANTA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Gandanta Dosha (birth at a water–fire sign junction — Pisces–Aries, Cancer–Leo, Scorpio–Sagittarius — or at the Revati–Ashwini and similar nakshatra junctions) fructifies chiefly in the first years of childhood and during transits over that junction. The window can bring childhood risk, fear for health, and distress to the parents. Gandanta shanti removes it.

GRAHAN_DOSHA.timing: Grahan Dosha acts intensely in the dasha of the Sun, Moon, Rahu or Ketu, and during eclipses.
GRAHAN_DOSHA.timingProse: The Grahan Dosha (the Sun or Moon conjoined with Rahu/Ketu) acts most intensely during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of those grahas, and during actual eclipses (solar or lunar). An eclipsed Sun signals erosion of the father's welfare and of vitality; an eclipsed Moon, erosion of the mother's welfare and of mental strength. Transits of Rahu/Ketu over the natal Sun or Moon bring the effect to the surface.

GURU_CHANDAL.timing: Guru-Chandal signals confusion of judgement and dharma during a Jupiter–Rahu dasha.
GURU_CHANDAL.timingProse: The Guru-Chandal yoga (Jupiter conjoined with Rahu) tends to act during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Jupiter and Rahu. This window can bring confused judgement, drift from dharma, friction with teachers, and attraction to unethical paths; yet with a strong Jupiter it can also grant unconventional, original attainment. A benefic Jupiter transit through its own, exaltation or a friendly sign eases the effect.

KALA_AMRITA_YOGA.timing: Kala Amrita Yoga (the auspicious form of Kalsarpa) signals delayed but exceptional results in the nodal dasha.
KALA_AMRITA_YOGA.timingProse: The Kala Amrita Yoga (all grahas enclosed from Ketu in the 1st to Rahu in the 7th — the auspicious form of Kalsarpa) fructifies during the dasha of Rahu and Ketu. The window brings delay and struggle at first, and thereafter (often after the age of 35) sudden, exceptional attainment and spiritual elevation. Met with patience, its fruit is sweet.

KALSARPA.timing: Kalsarpa fructifies strongly in the dasha of Rahu or Ketu and during Saturn transits.
KALSARPA.timingProse: The Kalsarpa Dosha acts most strongly during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Rahu and Ketu, when the affliction accumulated by all grahas being hemmed within the Rahu–Ketu axis comes to fruition. Saturn transits — especially the Sade Sati window from the natal Moon — and eclipse periods sharpen the effect. Life-struggle typically surfaces between the ages of about 25 and 36, easing gradually thereafter.

KALSARPA_ANANT.timing: Ananta Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 1st) signals obstacles to self and health in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_ANANT.timingProse: In the Ananta Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 1st and Ketu in the 7th. It fructifies during the Mahadasha/Antardasha of Rahu and Ketu, especially after the age of 25. The window can bring shaken self-confidence, health obstacles and marital friction; the Saturn Sade Sati sharpens it. It eases gradually with maturity.

KALSARPA_GHATAK.timing: Ghatak Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 10th) signals obstacles to career and status in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_GHATAK.timingProse: In the Ghatak Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 10th and Ketu in the 4th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring hindrance in the field of work, breaks in position and status, uncertainty in profession and friction with superiors — though a strong Rahu in the 10th can also drive political rise. Saturn transiting the 10th sharpens the effect.

KALSARPA_KARKOTAK.timing: Karkotak Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 8th) signals longevity, occult illness and sudden obstacles in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_KARKOTAK.timingProse: In the Karkotak Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 8th and Ketu in the 2nd. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring fear for longevity, hidden ailments, sudden obstacles and mental unrest — though it also suits attainment in the occult sciences. Saturn transiting the 8th sharpens the effect.

KALSARPA_KULIK.timing: Kulik Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 2nd) signals wealth, speech and family obstacles in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_KULIK.timingProse: In the Kulik Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 2nd and Ketu in the 8th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring obstacles to savings, troubles of speech, family discord and sudden expenditure. Saturn transiting the 2nd or 8th sharpens the effect.

KALSARPA_MAHAPADMA.timing: Mahapadma Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 6th) signals enemies, disease and debt in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_MAHAPADMA.timingProse: In the Mahapadma Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 6th and Ketu in the 12th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring affliction from enemies, disease, mounting debt and excessive expenditure — though a strong Rahu in the 6th can also confer victory over foes. Saturn transiting the 6th or 12th sharpens the effect.

KALSARPA_PADMA.timing: Padma Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 5th) signals obstacles to progeny and learning in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_PADMA.timingProse: In the Padma Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 5th and Ketu in the 11th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring delay in progeny, interruption of studies and confused judgement. Rahu transiting the 5th sharpens it; a strong 5th lord eases it.

KALSARPA_SHANKHACHUD.timing: Shankhachud Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 9th) signals obstacles to fortune, dharma and father in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_SHANKHACHUD.timingProse: In the Shankhachud Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 9th and Ketu in the 3rd. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring delay in fortune, confusion of dharma, distress to the father and hindrance in long journeys. Rahu transiting the 9th sharpens it; a strong Jupiter eases it.

KALSARPA_SHANKHPAL.timing: Shankhpal Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 4th) signals obstacles to mother and home in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_SHANKHPAL.timingProse: In the Shankhpal Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 4th and Ketu in the 10th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring obstacles to the comfort of the mother, troubles over home and vehicles, mental unrest and hindrance in the field of work. Kantaka Shani (Saturn transiting the 4th) sharpens the effect.

KALSARPA_SHESHNAG.timing: Sheshnag Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 12th) signals expenditure, exile and obstacles to liberation in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_SHESHNAG.timingProse: In the Sheshnag Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 12th and Ketu in the 6th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring excessive expenditure, broken sleep, fear of hidden enemies, residence abroad and mental unrest — though a 12th-house Rahu also suits the pursuit of liberation and spiritual discipline.

KALSARPA_TAKSHAK.timing: Takshak Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 7th) signals obstacles to marriage and partnership in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_TAKSHAK.timingProse: In the Takshak Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 7th and Ketu in the 1st. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu, especially around the age of marriage; the window can bring marital friction, discord in partnership, delay in marriage and connections abroad. Saturn transiting the 7th sharpens the effect.

KALSARPA_VASUKI.timing: Vasuki Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 3rd) signals obstacles to valour and siblings in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_VASUKI.timingProse: In the Vasuki Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 3rd and Ketu in the 9th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring obstacles to initiative, friction with siblings, delay in fortune and troubles in travel — though in enterprise Rahu lends unusual daring.

KALSARPA_VISHDHAR.timing: Vishdhar Kalsarpa (Rahu in the 11th) signals obstacles to gains, friends and desires in the nodal dasha.
KALSARPA_VISHDHAR.timingProse: In the Vishdhar Kalsarpa, Rahu sits in the 11th and Ketu in the 5th. It fructifies in the dasha of Rahu and Ketu; the window can bring delay in gains, friction with friends, hindrance in fulfilling desires, and a cycle of sudden gain and loss — though an 11th-house Rahu can also bring sudden large gains.

KEMDRUM_DOSHA.timing: Kemdrum Dosha shows mental distress and want during a Moon dasha and weak Moon transits.
KEMDRUM_DOSHA.timingProse: The Kemdrum Dosha (no planet in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon) acts chiefly during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of the Moon. Mental restlessness, isolation and financial strain grow during weak Moon transits and near the new Moon. If the Moon occupies a kendra or receives a benefic aspect a cancellation arises; otherwise the distress tends to appear in childhood or youth.

KENDRADHIPATI_DOSHA.timing: Kendradhipati Dosha signals reduced benefic results during the dasha of a benefic angular lord.
KENDRADHIPATI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Kendradhipati Dosha (a benefic losing its auspiciousness by ruling an angle) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of that benefic angular lord (Jupiter, Venus, etc.). The window can bring a reduction of expected benefic results, mixed outcomes, and uncertainty in enterprise. Another benefic association of the angular lord somewhat improves the result.

KRISHNA_PAKSHA_DOSHA.timing: Krishna-Paksha Dosha signals low mental strength during a Moon dasha and waning-Moon transits.
KRISHNA_PAKSHA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Krishna-Paksha Dosha (birth with a waning Moon in the dark fortnight) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of the Moon and during dark-fortnight transits. The window can bring low mental strength, lack of self-confidence, restlessness, and obstacles to the comfort of the mother. The bright fortnight, the period near the full Moon, and benefic associations ease it.

KUJA_BHANGA_ABSENT.timing: Absence of Kuja-bhanga signals an uncancelled, full Mangal Dosha during a Mars dasha.
KUJA_BHANGA_ABSENT.timingProse: The absence of Kuja-bhanga (no cancellation of the Mangal Dosha) shows during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Mars and around marriage. With no cancellation, the Mangal Dosha acts in full — marital distress and delay in marriage are the stronger. An equal dosha in both partners removes it; otherwise Mars transiting the 7th sharpens the effect.

MAHENDRA_ABSENCE.timing: Mahendra absence signals a lack of the auspicious lineage-and-progeny support after marriage.
MAHENDRA_ABSENCE.timingProse: The absence of Mahendra (the bride’s nakshatra not falling at the 4th, 7th, 10th, etc., count from the groom’s) shows after marriage. This is not a strong fault but an absence of benefit — merely the lack of the Mahendra blessing for longevity and growth of lineage and progeny. With other kootas strong, the result is ordinary.

MANGAL_DOSHA.timing: Mangal Dosha fructifies chiefly in a Mars dasha or transit, and especially around the age of marriage.
MANGAL_DOSHA.timingProse: The Mangal (Kuja) Dosha tends to act during the Mahadasha or Antardasha of Mars, and most visibly around marriageable age (roughly 24–30). Marital friction intensifies when Mars transits the 7th, 8th, or the Lagna from the natal Moon/Lagna. If an afflicted Mars also rules a period connected to the 7th lord, marriage may be delayed or strained. Where a Kuja-bhanga (cancellation) is present, the effect is substantially reduced.

MATRI_DOSHA.timing: Matri Dosha signals distress to the mother during the dasha of the 4th lord or Moon.
MATRI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Matri Dosha fructifies during the dasha of the 4th lord (lord of the mother) and the Moon (significator of the mother). The window can bring concern for the mother’s health, fear of separation from her, and obstacles to domestic comfort. A waning Moon transit, or the Moon transiting the 4th, sharpens it; a strong Moon and 4th lord ease it.

MOOL_DOSHA.timing: Mool Dosha signals risk near the parents in early childhood (especially the first year).
MOOL_DOSHA.timingProse: The Mool Dosha (birth in a Mula-class nakshatra — Mula, Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, Revati and the like) fructifies chiefly in the first years of childhood. The window can bring distress to the child’s health and, depending on the pada (quarter), an indication of risk to the parental line. Mula shanti (nakshatra japa after 27 days) removes it.

MRITYU_BHAGA_DOSHA.timing: Mrityu-Bhaga Dosha signals risk in the related house during that planet’s dasha.
MRITYU_BHAGA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Mrityu-Bhaga Dosha (a planet sitting at its "death-degree") fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of that planet. The window can bring risk connected with the house it signifies, distress to health, and hindrance in the matters it governs. Propitiation of the planet and strength of that house remove it.

NADI_DOSHA.timing: Nadi Dosha signals obstacles to progeny and health after marriage.
NADI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Nadi Dosha (the partners sharing the same Nadi — the heaviest fault in the Ashtakoota) fructifies after marriage, in the matter of progeny and health. The window can bring obstacles to conceiving, distress to marital health, and hindrance to the continuation of the lineage. A difference of Nadi, identity of sign lords, or a difference of nakshatra eases it.

NAGA_DOSHA.timing: Naga Dosha signals obstacles to progeny during a Rahu/Ketu or 5th-lord dasha.
NAGA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Naga Dosha (indicating a serpent-curse) tends to act during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Rahu and Ketu, and in the period of the 5th lord (lord of progeny). This window can bring delay in conceiving, obstacles to pregnancy, and concern for the health of children. Transits of Rahu/Ketu through the 5th bring the effect to the fore; Naga worship and serpent-propitiation rites bring relief.

PATNI_DOSHA.timing: Patni Dosha signals marital distress during the dasha of the 7th lord or Venus.
PATNI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Patni Dosha fructifies during the dasha of the 7th lord (lord of spouse) and Venus (significator of the wife), especially after marriage. The window can bring marital discord, concern for the spouse’s health, and fear of separation. Saturn transiting the 7th, or a weak Venus, sharpens it; a strong 7th lord and Venus ease it.

PITRA_DOSHA.timing: Pitra Dosha fructifies in the dasha of the Sun or Rahu and the 9th lord, and during eclipses.
PITRA_DOSHA.timingProse: Pitra Dosha tends to act during the Mahadasha or Antardasha of the Sun and Rahu, and in periods connected to the 9th lord (Bhagyesha) and the Sun as significator of the father. Solar eclipses, the Pitru-paksha fortnight, and Saturn transits intensify the ancestral debt. This window often marks obstacles to children, to the father's welfare, and to the continuation of the lineage; shraddha and tarpana rites bring relief.

PURNA_MANGAL.timing: Purna (full) Mangal Dosha signals strong marital friction during a Mars dasha and marriage.
PURNA_MANGAL.timingProse: The Purna (full) Mangal Dosha — a strong Kuja affliction — fructifies most intensely during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Mars and around marriageable age. The window can bring marital discord, delay in marriage and concern for the spouse’s health. Mars transiting the 7th or 8th sharpens it; when both partners carry an equal dosha it is mutually neutralised.

PUTRA_DOSHA.timing: Putra Dosha signals obstacles to progeny during the dasha of the 5th lord or Jupiter.
PUTRA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Putra Dosha fructifies during the dasha of the 5th lord (lord of progeny) and Jupiter (significator of children). The window can bring delay in conceiving, obstacles to pregnancy, and concern for the health of children. Transits of Rahu/Ketu through the 5th, or a weak Jupiter, sharpen it; a strong 5th lord and Jupiter bring the joy of children.

RAJJU_DOSHA.timing: Rajju Dosha signals obstacles to marital longevity through a shared Rajju after marriage.
RAJJU_DOSHA.timingProse: The Rajju Dosha (the partners’ nakshatras falling in the same Rajju strand) fructifies after marriage. The window can bring obstacles to marital longevity, fear of separation, and distress in shared life (the affected limb — head, neck, etc. — following the Rajju segment). A difference of Rajju and benefic strength ease it.

RIN_DOSHA_PITRI.timing: Pitri Rin Dosha signals ancestral (paternal) debt during the dasha of the Sun or 9th lord.
RIN_DOSHA_PITRI.timingProse: The Pitri Rin Dosha (ancestral debt of the paternal line) fructifies during the dasha of the Sun (significator of the father) and the 9th lord. The window can bring distress from the paternal-line debt, obstacles to the father’s welfare, a burden of duty, and causeless delay. Solar eclipses and the Pitru-paksha fortnight sharpen it; tarpana and shraddha rites bring relief.

RIN_DOSHA_STRI.timing: Stri Rin Dosha signals debt toward women during the dasha of Venus or the 7th lord.
RIN_DOSHA_STRI.timingProse: The Stri Rin Dosha (debt connected with women) fructifies during the dasha of Venus (significator of women) and the 7th lord. The window can bring distress from a debt connected with the feminine, marital obstacles, and hindrance indicating a woman’s grievance. A weak Venus, or Venus transiting the 7th, sharpens it; honouring women, charity and dharma bring relief.

RIN_DOSHA_SWAJAN.timing: Swajan Rin Dosha signals debt toward kin during the dasha of the 3rd or 11th lord.
RIN_DOSHA_SWAJAN.timingProse: The Swajan Rin Dosha (debt toward one’s own people) fructifies during the dasha of the 3rd lord (siblings) and the 11th lord (gains and kin). The window can bring distress from a debt connected with relatives, friction with siblings, and betrayal by helpers. Saturn transiting the 3rd or 11th sharpens it; service to kin and charity bring relief.

SANKRANTI_DOSHA.timing: Sankranti Dosha signals distress during a Sun dasha and Sankranti transit periods.
SANKRANTI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Sankranti Dosha (birth near the sacred moment of a solar Sankranti) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of the Sun and during Sankranti transit periods. The window can bring unsteady health, obstacles to the father’s welfare, and mixed results (varying by the type of Sankranti). Propitiation of the Sun and charity remove it.

SHANI_DOSHA.timing: Shani Dosha signals toil, delay and distress during a Saturn dasha and the Sade Sati.
SHANI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Shani Dosha acts chiefly during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Saturn, and most of all during the Sade Sati (the seven-and-a-half-year Saturn transit from the natal Moon) and Kantaka Shani (the 4th and 8th transit). This window brings heavy labour, delay, loss of position and separation from kin; yet, met with patience and steady work, it yields lasting results in the end.

SHRAPIT_DOSHA.timing: Shrapit Dosha (Saturn–Rahu) signals distress of past karma during a Saturn–Rahu dasha and the Sade Sati.
SHRAPIT_DOSHA.timingProse: The Shrapit Dosha (Saturn conjoined with Rahu, indicating a past-life curse) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Saturn and Rahu, and most of all during the Sade Sati. The window can bring prolonged delay, causeless distress, separation from kin, depression and a sense of karmic bondage. Patience, service, charity and dharma bring gradual relief.

STREE_DEERGH_ABSENCE.timing: Stree-Deergha absence signals a lack of the blessing for lasting marital happiness.
STREE_DEERGH_ABSENCE.timingProse: The absence of Stree-Deergha (the bride’s nakshatra not falling beyond the 9th count from the groom’s) shows after marriage. It indicates an absence of benefit — merely the lack of the Stree-Deergha blessing for the durability of marital happiness, not a strong fault. With sign-lord friendship and planetary strength, the result is ordinary.

TITHI_DOSHA.timing: Tithi Dosha (Rikta/Kshaya tithi birth) signals obstruction to auspicious work on that tithi.
TITHI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Tithi Dosha (birth on a Rikta, Kshaya or Dagdha tithi) fructifies at the start of auspicious undertakings and during the transit of that tithi. The window can bring obstruction to auspicious work, delay at the outset, and broken resolve. Choosing an auspicious tithi and muhurta removes it.

VAIDHRITI_DOSHA.timing: Vaidhriti Yoga Dosha signals obstruction to auspicious work during that yoga’s transit.
VAIDHRITI_DOSHA.timingProse: The Vaidhriti Yoga Dosha (birth in an inauspicious yoga such as Vaidhriti or Vyatipata) fructifies at the start of auspicious undertakings and during the transit of that yoga. The window can bring obstruction to auspicious work, sudden hindrance, and disturbed resolve. Yoga shanti and choosing an auspicious muhurta remove it.

VEDHA_DOSHA.timing: Vedha Dosha signals distress through mutually obstructing nakshatras after marriage.
VEDHA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Vedha Dosha (a mutual piercing/obstruction between the partners’ nakshatras) fructifies after marriage. The window can bring mutual obstruction, causeless opposition and hindrance to shared life. Friendship between the lords of the piercing nakshatras and benefic associations ease it.

VISHA_KANYA_DOSHA.timing: Visha-Kanya Dosha signals marital and spousal risk after marriage.
VISHA_KANYA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Visha-Kanya Dosha (birth in an inauspicious tithi–weekday–nakshatra combination) fructifies after marriage, within married life. The window can bring marital discord, concern for the spouse’s health, and obstacles to conjugal happiness. Benefic associations, planetary strength and propitiation reduce the fault; note that this dosha is contested today and rejected by many.

VISH_YOGA_DOSHA.timing: Vish Yoga (Saturn–Moon) signals melancholy and despondency during a Saturn–Moon dasha.
VISH_YOGA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Vish Yoga Dosha (Saturn conjoined with the Moon) fructifies during the Mahadasha and Antardasha of Saturn and the Moon, and during the Sade Sati. The window can bring mental melancholy, despondency, isolation, loss of enthusiasm and disorders of phlegm and wind. A benefic Moon transit and the aspect of Jupiter ease it.

VYATIPATA_DOSHA.timing: Vyatipata Yoga Dosha signals sudden obstruction to auspicious work during that yoga’s transit.
VYATIPATA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Vyatipata Yoga Dosha (birth in the 17th, Vyatipata yoga) fructifies at the start of auspicious undertakings and during the Vyatipata transit. The window can bring sudden obstruction, fear of accident, and broken resolve. Yoga shanti and choosing an auspicious muhurta remove it.

YAMAGHANTA_DOSHA.timing: Yamaghanta Dosha signals obstruction to auspicious work during that weekday-nakshatra yoga.
YAMAGHANTA_DOSHA.timingProse: The Yamaghanta Dosha (birth in an inauspicious weekday–nakshatra combination, the Yamaghanta yoga) fructifies at the start of auspicious undertakings and during the transit of that yoga. The window can bring obstruction to auspicious work, hindrance in travel, and sudden distress. Choosing an auspicious muhurta and yoga shanti remove it.

DEVA.phala: Deva gana denotes a sattvic, gentle and dharmic temperament.
DEVA.phalaProse: The Deva (divine) gana comprises nine nakshatras — Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Shravana and Revati. A person born under it is of a sattvic nature: gentle, benevolent, straightforward, forgiving and drawn to dharmic observance. They are calm-minded, disciplined and measured in speech, with little anger or greed. In Gana koota (worth 6 of the 8 koota points), Deva-Deva is the best match and Deva-Manushya is moderate, while Deva-Rakshasa is the most inauspicious pairing and breeds discord.

MANUSHYA.phala: Manushya gana denotes a rajasic, balanced and ambitious human temperament.
MANUSHYA.phalaProse: The Manushya (human) gana comprises nine nakshatras — Bharani, Rohini, Ardra, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, Uttara Ashadha, Purva Bhadrapada and Uttara Bhadrapada. A person born under it has a rajasic nature, balancing material and spiritual aims; ambitious yet moral, practical and socially engaged. In Gana koota, Manushya-Manushya is the best match, Deva-Manushya is auspicious, and Manushya-Rakshasa yields only partial harmony.

RAKSHASA.phala: Rakshasa gana denotes a tamasic, strong-willed and dominating temperament.
RAKSHASA.phalaProse: The Rakshasa gana comprises nine nakshatras — Krittika, Ashlesha, Magha, Chitra, Vishakha, Jyeshtha, Mula, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha. A person born under it is of a tamasic nature: strong-willed, blunt, independent and dominating, sometimes aggressive or obstinate, yet fearless, courageous and quick to resist injustice. In Gana koota, Rakshasa-Rakshasa is tolerable and Manushya-Rakshasa is moderate, while Deva-Rakshasa is the most inauspicious pairing and breeds discord.

JUPITER_IN_1.name: Jupiter in Lagna: Raja Yoga. Wisdom, dharma, longevity, dignified persona, guru's grace per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in Lagna confers wisdom, religiosity, longevity, a dignified persona, and natural teacher-student affection. BPHS Ch.21 ranks this among the highest Raja-yoga placements — the kāraka of jñāna in the body-bhava grants self-purification, learning growth, and guru's grace as life-long fixtures. The native often becomes a counselor, teacher, or moral authority within their circle.
JUPITER_IN_1.general: Raja Yoga, wisdom, dharmic disposition, longevity, dignified persona, guru's grace, scriptural learning.

JUPITER_IN_10.name: Jupiter in 10th: kāraka-kendra Raja Yoga. High office, dharmic profession, royal honour per Phaladeepika 8.
JUPITER_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 10th forms a kāraka-kendra Raja Yoga — high office, dharmic profession (teaching, religion, law, philosophy, judiciary), royal recognition, and untarnished reputation. BPHS Ch.21 — kāraka-kendra union confers elevated career fruits. Common in judges, professors, and ethical statesmen.
JUPITER_IN_10.general: Kāraka-kendra Raja Yoga, high office, dharmic profession, royal recognition, untarnished reputation.

JUPITER_IN_11.name: Jupiter in 11th: Lābha-Dharma Yoga. Continuous wealth, dharmic friend-family per Phaladeepika 8.
JUPITER_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 11th forms a Lābha-Dharma Yoga — continuous wealth growth, dharmic friend-circles, and steady fulfilment of desires. BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in the gain-bhava augments all life-domains. Common in those whose income flows from dharmic work or who become philanthropists in later life.
JUPITER_IN_11.general: Lābha-Dharma Yoga, continuous wealth, dharmic friend-family, desire-fulfilment, elder sibling support.

JUPITER_IN_12.name: Jupiter in 12th: Mokṣa Yoga, charitable, pilgrim, but heavy (dharmic) expenditure per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 12th forms a Mokṣa Yoga — charitable and dharmic, dwelling at sacred places/ashrams, spending on spiritual ends, and earning religious fame abroad. BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in the vyaya-bhava is the significator of liberation: it turns expenditure toward dharma and charity and grants a good final passage. The expenditure is heavy, but channelled into worthy religious causes.
JUPITER_IN_12.general: Mokṣa Yoga, charity, pilgrimage/ashram life, spiritual expenditure, good final passage.

JUPITER_IN_2.name: Jupiter in 2nd: Dhana-Vāk Yoga. Prosperity, truthful sweet speech, family support per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 2nd forms a Dhana-Vāk Yoga — prosperity, sweet and truthful speech, family nourishment, and higher education. BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in the wealth-bhava augments all assets and joins learning with wealth. The speech carries dharma and truth; the native often supports the extended family. Common in teachers, advisors, and ethically-wealthy householders.
JUPITER_IN_2.general: Prosperity, truthful sweet speech, family support, higher education, Dhana-Vāk Yoga.

JUPITER_IN_3.name: Jupiter in 3rd: dharmic effort, sibling happiness, mild kāraka-dimming per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 3rd makes the native dharmic in effort, happy in siblings, and inclined to teach and advise. BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter is slightly subdued in this upachaya (the great benefic gives less in the labour/prowess houses), yet it grants a dharma-communicating disposition, sound counsel, and younger-sibling comfort. Being an upachaya, its fruits build with time. Wisdom expressed through enterprise and writing.
JUPITER_IN_3.general: Dharmic effort, sibling happiness, counsel/teaching, gradual growth, mild kāraka-dimming.

JUPITER_IN_4.name: Jupiter in 4th: maternal happiness, home, vehicles, dharmic householder, heart-peace per Phaladeepika 8.
JUPITER_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 4th confers maternal happiness, ample home and vehicles, a dharmic householder disposition, and inner contentment. BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in the comfort-bhava forms a kendra-kāraka union, augmenting domestic prosperity and ancestral property. Often produces those who manage family religious institutions or ancestral land.
JUPITER_IN_4.general: Maternal happiness, home/vehicles, dharmic householder, heart-peace, ancestral property growth.

JUPITER_IN_5.name: Jupiter in 5th: kāraka-kāraka Raja Yoga. Progeny, mantra-siddhi, learning, fame per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 5th forms a kāraka-kāraka Raja Yoga — Jupiter (kāraka of progeny + wisdom) in the bhava of progeny + past-merit. The native enjoys progeny, mantra-siddhi, learning, and royal fame. BPHS Ch.21 ranks this as one of the supreme placements; common in spiritual teachers, scholars, and dharmic statesmen.
JUPITER_IN_5.general: Kāraka-kāraka Raja Yoga, progeny, mantra-siddhi, learning, royal fame.

JUPITER_IN_6.name: Jupiter in 6th: subdues enemies, wins disputes by dharma, but kāraka-dimming per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 6th lets the native subdue enemies through righteousness, win disputes, and clear debts, but it signals a kāraka-loss for Jupiter (the great benefic afflicted in a dusthāna). BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in the foe-bhava dispels enemies by the force of justice and dharma, conferring standing in medicine/law/service, while its own auspicious gifts dim slightly. Being an upachaya, victory accrues over time.
JUPITER_IN_6.general: Subdues enemies, wins disputes, clears debt, standing in service/law, mild kāraka-dimming.

JUPITER_IN_7.name: Jupiter in 7th: dharmic spousal yoga, learned partner, ethical business per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 7th confers a dharmic spousal yoga — a learned/scholarly partner, ethical business, and gainful foreign travel. BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in kalatra-bhava produces a religiously-inclined spouse and ethical business conduct. Caveat: in rare configurations, the placement's dharmic pull can manifest as celibacy/late-marriage when Jupiter dominates the bhava without other relationship indicators.
JUPITER_IN_7.general: Dharmic spousal yoga, scholarly partner, ethical business, foreign travel gains, fame via marriage.

JUPITER_IN_8.name: Jupiter in 8th: longevity, occult-scriptural knowledge, inheritance, but kāraka-dimming per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
JUPITER_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 8th confers longevity, knowledge of occult/metaphysical scripture, and sudden gains through inheritance/legacy, but signals a loss to Jupiter’s benefic significance (the great benefic in the randhra-dusthāna). BPHS Ch.21 — Jupiter in the longevity-bhava extends life, inclines toward mokṣa-scripture, and favours inheritance/insurance/trust gains, while domestic ease and fortune dim a little. Benefic aspect yields a longevity-and-legacy yoga.
JUPITER_IN_8.general: Longevity, occult/scriptural knowledge, inheritance, mokṣa-leaning, mild kāraka-dimming.

JUPITER_IN_9.name: Jupiter in 9th: supreme Dharma Raja Yoga (kāraka-kāraka-trikoṇa). Highest fortune per Phaladeepika 8.
JUPITER_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Jupiter in the 9th forms the supreme Dharma Raja Yoga — kāraka-kāraka-trikoṇa, where Jupiter (kāraka of dharma + fortune) sits in the dharma-bhava itself. The native enjoys the highest fortune, deep guru's grace, mastery of scriptures, and unwavering dharmic disposition. BPHS Ch.21 calls this the most celebrated of all Jupiter placements. Signature of legendary saints, scholars, and just rulers.
JUPITER_IN_9.general: Supreme Dharma Raja Yoga, highest fortune, guru's grace, scriptural mastery, dharmic life.

KETU_IN_1.name: Ketu in 1st: self-doubt, detachment, intuitive depth, head/skin sensitivity per BPHS.
KETU_IN_1.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in Lagna gives self-doubt, an introverted and detached disposition, intuitive depth, but a tendency to confusion about self-identity. Ketu as the significator of liberation in the body-bhava brings worldly non-attachment, possible head/skin issues, and an attraction to secret knowledge. Under benefic aspect it yields a spiritual-insight yoga; afflicted, it lowers self-confidence and clarity of identity.
KETU_IN_1.general: Self-doubt, detachment, intuitive depth, head/skin sensitivity, spirituality.

KETU_IN_10.name: Ketu in 10th: unconventional career, detachment from results, occult/research profession per BPHS.
KETU_IN_10.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 10th inclines the native to an unconventional career, detachment from career-results, skill in occult-research/tantra/astrology/medical professions, but instability of fame. Ketu in the karma-bhava brings past-life-honed competence, sudden career changes, and indifference to reputation. Under benefic aspect it forms an esoteric-knowledge-career/fame yoga; afflicted, career instability and fluctuating standing.
KETU_IN_10.general: Unconventional career, detachment from results, occult/research profession, fluctuating fame, innate competence.

KETU_IN_11.name: Ketu in 11th: sudden gains, unconventional friends, detachment from desires, esoteric network per BPHS.
KETU_IN_11.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 11th is a favourable placement — sudden gains, an unconventional/esoteric friend-circle, and detachment from the pursuit of desires. Ketu in the gain-bhava is strong by being an upachaya: it gives connection to spiritual/occult communities, unexpected income, or coolness with the elder sibling. This is one of Ketu’s good houses. Under benefic aspect it forms a sudden-gain yoga; afflicted, fluctuating gains and aloofness from friends.
KETU_IN_11.general: Sudden gains, unconventional friends, detachment from desires, esoteric network, unexpected income.

KETU_IN_12.name: Ketu in 12th: supreme Mokṣa Yoga (kāraka-kāraka). Liberation-aptitude, subtle vision per BPHS 29.
KETU_IN_12.prose: Per BPHS Ch.29, Ketu in the 12th forms the supreme Mokṣa Yoga — kāraka-kāraka where Ketu (the mokṣa-significator) sits in the mokṣa-bhava itself. The native enjoys liberation-aptitude, subtle/visionary perception, foreign residence, sattvic renunciation, and fame for hidden charity. Phaladeepika Ch.8 — the supreme Ketu placement. Signature of saints, mystics, and ego-transcendent souls.
KETU_IN_12.general: Supreme Mokṣa Yoga, liberation-aptitude, subtle vision, foreign residence, sattvic renunciation, hidden charity.

KETU_IN_2.name: Ketu in 2nd: detached speech, financial uncertainty, mantra/speech-siddhi, family aloofness per BPHS.
KETU_IN_2.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 2nd gives sparse or cryptic speech, a detached and uncertain attitude to wealth, yet a proneness to mantra/speech-siddhi. Ketu in the wealth-bhava brings indifference to accumulation, coolness in family ties, and possible mouth/dietary issues. Under benefic aspect it yields a mantra/tantra speech-perfection yoga; afflicted, it brings financial fluctuation and speech defects.
KETU_IN_2.general: Detached speech, financial uncertainty, mantra/speech-siddhi, family aloofness, dietary issues.

KETU_IN_3.name: Ketu in 3rd: fearless valour, cryptic communication skill, aloofness from siblings per BPHS.
KETU_IN_3.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 3rd gives fearless valour, skill in cryptic/technical communication and writing, intuitive insight, but a coolness toward siblings. Ketu in this upachaya raises courage, subtle reasoning, and a pull toward secret/esoteric knowledge — being an upachaya, a favourable placement for the node. Under benefic aspect it forms an investigation-and-valour yoga; afflicted, it brings friction with siblings and restlessness.
KETU_IN_3.general: Fearless valour, cryptic communication skill, intuition, aloofness from siblings, subtle reasoning.

KETU_IN_4.name: Ketu in 4th: detachment from home, mother-separation concern, inward search for peace per BPHS.
KETU_IN_4.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 4th brings detachment from home comforts, coolness or separation-concern regarding the mother, and an inward search for peace. Ketu in the comfort-bhava produces indifference to worldly domestic ease, relocation, or inner discontent, yet a thirst for spiritual peace and esoteric practice within the home. Under benefic aspect it gives an inner-peace/mokṣa yoga; afflicted, home unrest and difficulty for the mother.
KETU_IN_4.general: Detachment from home, mother-separation concern, inward search for peace, relocation, spirituality.

KETU_IN_5.name: Ketu in 5th: mantra-siddhi, esoteric intelligence, progeny concern, past-life impressions per BPHS.
KETU_IN_5.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 5th gives a proneness to mantra/tantra perfection, esoteric intelligence and intuition, strong past-life impressions, but concern or delay regarding children. Ketu as the significator of past-merit and mokṣa in the progeny-bhava grants spiritual intellect, yet disturbs the significator of offspring (risk of miscarriage or delay). Under benefic aspect it forms a mantra-siddhi/wisdom yoga; afflicted, difficulty with children.
KETU_IN_5.general: Mantra-siddhi, esoteric intelligence, progeny concern, past-life impressions, spiritual intellect.

KETU_IN_6.name: Ketu in 6th: destroys enemies, skilled in diagnosis/healing, conquers debt per BPHS.
KETU_IN_6.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 6th is a favourable placement — it destroys enemies, gives skill in diagnosis and esoteric healing, and conquers debts and rivals. Ketu in the foe-bhava is strong by being an upachaya: it grants subtle diagnostic insight, tantra/mantra-based healing, and competitive victory. This is one of Ketu’s best houses. Under benefic aspect it yields a physician/tantric-research yoga; afflicted, it raises the risk of abdominal/hidden ailments.
KETU_IN_6.general: Destroys enemies, diagnostic/healing skill, conquers debt, esoteric medicine, competitive victory.

KETU_IN_7.name: Ketu in 7th: marital detachment, relationship dispassion, mystical partner, business indifference per BPHS.
KETU_IN_7.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 7th indicates detachment in marriage, dispassion in relationships, a spouse of secretive/introverted nature, or delayed marriage. Ketu in the partnership-bhava produces indifference to worldly marital pleasure, aloofness in partnerships, or a tendency toward private relationships. Under benefic aspect it gives a spiritual-companion yoga; afflicted, marital coolness and fear of separation. Conscious engagement is the corrective.
KETU_IN_7.general: Marital detachment, relationship dispassion, mystical partner, delayed marriage, business indifference.

KETU_IN_8.name: Ketu in 8th: occult/yoga-siddhi, mokṣa-leaning, sudden events, longevity-mystery concern per BPHS.
KETU_IN_8.prose: Per BPHS, Ketu in the 8th makes the native prone to occult/tantra/yoga-perfection, a seeker of liberation, gifted with intuitive vision, but with proneness to sudden events and hidden longevity concern. Ketu as the significator of mokṣa in the randhra-bhava grants kundalini-yoga and esoteric-knowledge perfection (some hold it Ketu’s most auspicious house), yet a fear of abrupt change. Under benefic aspect it forms a yoga-siddhi/mokṣa yoga; afflicted, risk of accidents and hidden disease.
KETU_IN_8.general: Occult/yoga-siddhi, mokṣa-leaning, sudden events, longevity-mystery concern, kundalini-yoga.

KETU_IN_9.name: Ketu in 9th: Mokṣa-Dharma Yoga. Spiritual disposition, guru-grace, deep insight per BPHS 29.
KETU_IN_9.prose: Per BPHS Ch.29, Ketu in the 9th forms a Mokṣa-Dharma Yoga — spiritual disposition, guru-grace, deep insight, mastery of subtle scriptures, and past-life recall. Phaladeepika Ch.8 — Ketu's 9th-house placement is exceptionally auspicious for spiritual life. Common in mystics, esoteric scholars, and those whose dharmic life is interior rather than performative.
KETU_IN_9.general: Mokṣa-Dharma Yoga, spiritual disposition, guru's grace, deep insight, esoteric scriptural mastery.

MARS_IN_1.name: Mars in 1st: forceful, courageous, fiery temper, scar-marked; Maṅgalik yoga per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in Lagna makes the native forceful, courageous, leadership-prone, with a sharp temper and often a scar or mark on the body. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the body-bhava strengthens vitality but raises Maṅgalik (Kuja) dosha, asking effort for marital harmony. When Mars is exalted or in its own sign, the aggression matures into genuine leadership; when afflicted, impulsiveness and conflict dominate.
MARS_IN_1.general: Forcefulness, courage, leadership, fiery temper, impulsiveness, Maṅgalik yoga.

MARS_IN_10.name: Mars in 10th: dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga. Military leadership, intense effort, royal honour per Phaladeepika 8.
MARS_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 10th forms a special Karma Raja Yoga — Mars in the karma-bhava is dig-balī (directionally strong), conferring military/leadership capability, intense work-ethic, royal recognition, and heroic fame. BPHS Ch.24 — dig-balī Mars augments career fame. Common in generals, surgeons, athletes, and high-action executives.
MARS_IN_10.general: Dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga, military leadership, intense effort, royal recognition, heroic fame.

MARS_IN_11.name: Mars in 11th: Lābha-Śaurya Yoga. Courage-driven gains, elder-sibling growth per Phaladeepika 8.
MARS_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 11th forms a Lābha-Śaurya Yoga — courage-driven gains, elder-sibling growth, and entrepreneurial desire-fulfilment. BPHS Ch.24 — Mars in the gain-bhava augments all life-domains. Common in self-made entrepreneurs and competitive-industry leaders.
MARS_IN_11.general: Lābha-Śaurya Yoga, courage-driven gains, elder-sibling growth, entrepreneurial drive, desire-fulfilment.

MARS_IN_12.name: Mars in 12th: heavy expenditure, hidden enemies, weapon/fire losses; Maṅgalik yoga per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 12th tends toward heavy expenditure, affliction from hidden enemies, reduced bed-comfort, and losses through weapons/fire/accidents. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the vyaya-bhava spends energy, brings anger-born loss, and carries Maṅgalik (Kuja) dosha. Yet gains can come through valour abroad and proficiency in covert work, defence, or surgery. Benefic aspect reins in the expenditure and turns the drive constructive.
MARS_IN_12.general: Heavy expenditure, hidden enemies, reduced bed-comfort, valour abroad, Maṅgalik yoga.

MARS_IN_2.name: Mars in 2nd: harsh speech, family discord, wealth via daring; Maṅgalik yoga per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 2nd produces harsh speech, a tendency to family discord, and wealth earned through daring or hard work. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the wealth-bhava sharpens the tongue, heats the diet, and raises Maṅgalik (Kuja) dosha. Income tends to flow from land, metals, machinery, surgery, or armed/technical professions. A well-dignified Mars channels the force into enterprise rather than quarrel.
MARS_IN_2.general: Harsh speech, family discord, wealth via daring, land/metal trade, Maṅgalik yoga.

MARS_IN_3.name: Mars in 3rd: Parākrama Yoga (kāraka-kāraka). Heroic valour, sibling power, self-effort per Phaladeepika 8.
MARS_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 3rd forms a Parākrama Yoga — kāraka-kāraka where Mars (kāraka of valour + siblings) sits in parākrama-bhava itself. The native enjoys heroic valour, powerful siblings, self-effort prosperity, and entrepreneurial drive. BPHS Ch.24 — Mars yields supreme effects only in upachaya bhavas (3/6/10/11). Common in soldiers, athletes, and self-made entrepreneurs.
MARS_IN_3.general: Parākrama Yoga, heroic valour, sibling power, self-effort prosperity, entrepreneurial drive.

MARS_IN_4.name: Mars in 4th: domestic unrest, mother’s difficulty, property struggles; Maṅgalik yoga per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 4th tends toward domestic unrest, reduced maternal comfort, struggles over property/vehicles, and inner heat. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars works against the kāraka grain in the comfort-bhava (it opposes the comfort-significator Moon), eroding home-peace and prompting changes of residence; it also carries Maṅgalik (Kuja) dosha. Yet land, real-estate, and metals/machinery business can be a strong source of gain. A dignified Mars builds rather than disrupts the home.
MARS_IN_4.general: Domestic unrest, mother’s difficulty, property struggles, frequent relocation, Maṅgalik yoga.

MARS_IN_5.name: Mars in 5th: sharp intellect, effort for progeny, daring, competitive winner per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 5th gives sharp intellect, daring, and competitive success, but tends to bring difficulty or delay regarding children. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the progeny-bhava heats the mind, grants skill in mathematics/engineering and speculative courage, yet disturbs the significator of offspring — so effort is needed to protect progeny. A dignified Mars turns the intellectual fire toward leadership and strategy.
MARS_IN_5.general: Sharp intellect, competitive success, speculative daring, effort for progeny, math/engineering skill.

MARS_IN_6.name: Mars in 6th: enemy-victory yoga. Disease-conquest, debt-cancellation, physical strength per Phaladeepika 8.
MARS_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 6th forms a Vipareeta-style enemy-victory yoga — Mars's aggressive energy in the enemy-bhava conquers enemies, defeats disease, and cancels debt. BPHS Ch.24 — Mars in the 6th (an upachaya) is exceptionally strength-conferring. Common in athletes, military personnel, and litigators.
MARS_IN_6.general: Enemy-victory, disease-conquest, debt-cancellation, physical strength, courage.

MARS_IN_7.name: Mars in 7th: marital strife, strong Maṅgalik dosha, forceful partner per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 7th is a strong Maṅgalik (Kuja) dosha placement — it indicates marital strife, clashes of will, or delayed marriage. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the partnership-bhava gives the spouse a forceful, independent temperament and the native business-courage, but harmony asks conscious effort. The dosha is cancelled or eased when both charts carry matching Mars, when Mars is exalted/own-sign, or when the marriage-significator Venus/Jupiter aspects the 7th.
MARS_IN_7.general: Marital strife, Maṅgalik dosha, delayed marriage, forceful partner, business courage.

MARS_IN_8.name: Mars in 8th: longevity caution, weapon/fire risk, blood disorders; Maṅgalik yoga per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 8th raises caution about longevity, risk from weapons/fire/accidents, blood-and-bile disorders, and an angry streak. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the randhra-bhava is a maraka-class indicator and gives a capacity for surgery and deep research; it also carries Maṅgalik (Kuja) dosha. Yet a dignified Mars excels in surgery, forensics, and investigative fields, and benefic aspects materially temper the maraka force.
MARS_IN_8.general: Longevity caution, weapon/fire/accident risk, blood disorders, surgical/research aptitude, Maṅgalik yoga.

MARS_IN_9.name: Mars in 9th: enterprising fortune, friction with father, military/strategic skill per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MARS_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mars in the 9th makes the native enterprising and fortunate through effort, a defender of dharma, and skilled in military/strategy, though prone to friction with the father or guru-figures. BPHS Ch.23 — Mars in the fortune-trine raises fortune through valour and a martial/righteous-cause disposition, with strong opinions on doctrine. A dignified Mars gives leadership of armies or causes; an afflicted one harms paternal comfort.
MARS_IN_9.general: Enterprising fortune, defence of dharma, military/strategic skill, friction with father, valour-driven rise.

MERCURY_IN_1.name: Mercury in Lagna: eloquence, intellect, wit, youthful presence per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MERCURY_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in Lagna confers eloquence, intellect, wit, a youthful presence, and skill in mathematics/sciences. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in the body-bhava grants quick intelligence and communication skill. Common in writers, journalists, mathematicians, and analytic professionals.
MERCURY_IN_1.general: Eloquence, intellect, wit, youthful presence, mathematical/scientific skill.

MERCURY_IN_10.name: Mercury in 10th: Karma-Vāk Raja Yoga. Career fame via intellect/communication per Phaladeepika 8.
MERCURY_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 10th forms a Karma-Vāk Raja Yoga — kāraka-kendra union. Career fame through intellect and communication, royal recognition, and high office. BPHS Ch.23 — career-significator joining career-bhava. Common in journalists, consultants, executives, and analytic-profession leaders.
MERCURY_IN_10.general: Karma-Vāk Raja Yoga, intellect-communication fame, royal recognition, high office, business reputation.

MERCURY_IN_11.name: Mercury in 11th: Lābha-Vāk Yoga. Continuous business gains, network-driven income per Phaladeepika 8.
MERCURY_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 11th forms a Lābha-Vāk Yoga — continuous business gains, friend-network communication skill, speculation profits, and steady desire-fulfilment. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in the gain-bhava augments all life-domains. Common in network-dependent businesses (sales, brokerage, journalism).
MERCURY_IN_11.general: Lābha-Vāk Yoga, continuous business gains, network communication, speculation profits, desire-fulfilment.

MERCURY_IN_12.name: Mercury in 12th: managing expenses, confidential writing, reserved, foreign dealings per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
