MERCURY_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 12th makes the native expense-conscious, skilled in confidential/behind-the-scenes writing, reserved in speech, yet imaginative. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in the vyaya-bhava lowers overt communication-significance but supports foreign trade/correspondence and quiet research/writing. When afflicted, speech becomes hesitant; with benefic aspect it grants fame through writing produced abroad or in seclusion.
MERCURY_IN_12.general: Expense management, confidential writing, reserved speech, foreign dealings, imagination.

MERCURY_IN_2.name: Mercury in 2nd: Vāk-Dhana Yoga. Sweet speech, business acumen, family support per Phaladeepika 8.
MERCURY_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 2nd forms a Vāk-Dhana Yoga — sweet speech, family support, wealth via business acumen, and a charming presentation. BPHS Ch.23 — speech-kāraka in the wealth-bhava produces income through articulation. Common in salesmen, traders, brokers, and those whose speech is their livelihood.
MERCURY_IN_2.general: Vāk-Dhana Yoga, sweet speech, business acumen, family support, charming manner.

MERCURY_IN_3.name: Mercury in 3rd: writing/communication skill, sibling happiness, intellectual prowess per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MERCURY_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 3rd grants writing and communication skill, sibling happiness, intellectual prowess, and multi-talented dexterity. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in this upachaya amplifies its communication-significance, giving editing/journalism/trade skill and many friends. Being an upachaya placement, its fruits grow with time. A natural placement for writers, editors, marketers, and traders.
MERCURY_IN_3.general: Writing skill, communication dexterity, sibling happiness, intellectual prowess, versatility.

MERCURY_IN_4.name: Mercury in 4th: Vidyā-Gṛha Yoga. Maternal happiness, scholarly householder per Phaladeepika 8.
MERCURY_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 4th forms a Vidyā-Gṛha Yoga — maternal happiness, scholarly householder disposition, ample home/vehicles, and ethical manners. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in the comfort-bhava augments learning and domestic harmony. Common in academics whose home is their library.
MERCURY_IN_4.general: Vidyā-Gṛha Yoga, maternal happiness, home/vehicles, ethical manner, heart-peace.

MERCURY_IN_5.name: Mercury in 5th: Prajñā Raja Yoga (kāraka-trikoṇa). Intellect, speculation skill per Phaladeepika 8.
MERCURY_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 5th forms a Prajñā Raja Yoga — kāraka-trikoṇa where the learning-significator joins past-merit. The native enjoys keen intellect, mantra-siddhi, speculation/share-market skill, mathematical fame, and progeny happiness. BPHS Ch.23 — vidyā-kāraka fructifying through poorva-punya. Common in mathematicians, financial analysts, and skilled speculators.
MERCURY_IN_5.general: Prajñā Raja Yoga, mantra-siddhi, speculation skill, mathematical fame, progeny happiness.

MERCURY_IN_6.name: Mercury in 6th: wins debates, medical/accounting skill, but nervous strain per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MERCURY_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 6th makes the native victorious in debate/litigation, skilled in medicine and mathematics, and adept in service fields, though prone to nervous or skin-related strain. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in this upachaya grants triumph over enemies through argument, analytical skill, and accounting/auditing proficiency; over-thinking can weaken the nerves. Being an upachaya, success accrues steadily.
MERCURY_IN_6.general: Debate victory, medical/accounting skill, service proficiency, analysis, nervous strain.

MERCURY_IN_7.name: Mercury in 7th: Vyāpāra-Kalatra Yoga. Intelligent partner, partnership business per Phaladeepika 8.
MERCURY_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 7th forms a Vyāpāra-Kalatra Yoga — intelligent partner, business acumen, partnership-driven growth, and gainful travel. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in kalatra-bhava augments business speech and contract-making. Common in joint-venture entrepreneurs and partnership-business heirs.
MERCURY_IN_7.general: Vyāpāra-Kalatra Yoga, intelligent partner, partnership skill, gainful travel, ethical business.

MERCURY_IN_8.name: Mercury in 8th: skilled in occult/research, investigative, nervous/speech worry per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MERCURY_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 8th makes the native skilled in occult knowledge and research — astrology, tantra, mathematics, deep inquiry — though prone to nervous weakness and speech-related worry. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in the randhra-bhava grants profound investigative power and access to hidden knowledge, but can magnify anxiety or hesitation in expression. Longevity is often supported. With benefic aspect it yields a researcher/scientist yoga.
MERCURY_IN_8.general: Occult/research skill, investigative power, hidden knowledge, nervous/speech worry, longevity.

MERCURY_IN_9.name: Mercury in 9th: learned in scripture, philosophical, fortunate, a teacher per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 23.
MERCURY_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Mercury in the 9th makes the native learned in scripture, skilled in philosophy/doctrine, fortunate, and a good teacher/advisor. BPHS Ch.23 — Mercury in the fortune-trine unites intellect with dharma, giving reasoned religious knowledge, writing and oratory skill, and gainful travel. A Mercury–Jupiter link here raises scholarship to its peak — common in academics, commentators, and dharmic communicators.
MERCURY_IN_9.general: Scriptural learning, philosophical skill, rise of fortune, teaching ability, writing/oratory.

MOON_IN_1.name: Moon in Lagna: emotionally rich, fair-complexioned, mother-bonded, sensorially abundant per Phaladeepika 8.
MOON_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Moon in Lagna confers emotional richness, fair complexion, strong mother-bond, sensory abundance, and sensitivity. BPHS Ch.22 — many Bhāva-kāraka yogas form from Chandra-Lagna (the Moon as auxiliary ascendant for relationship-/emotion-domain readings). Common in caregivers, hospitality professionals, and emotionally-attuned creatives.
MOON_IN_1.general: Emotional richness, fair complexion, mother-bond, sensory abundance, sensitivity.

MOON_IN_10.name: Moon in 10th: Karma-Kāraka Raja Yoga. Public-favoured career, entertainment industry per Phaladeepika 8.
MOON_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Moon in the 10th forms a Karma-Kāraka Raja Yoga — public-favoured career, entertainment-industry success, mother-career synergy, and intense work-output. BPHS Ch.22 — Moon in karma-bhava augments public-recognition fame. Common in entertainers, hospitality professionals, and politicians whose appeal is mass-emotional.
MOON_IN_10.general: Karma-Kāraka Raja Yoga, public-favoured career, entertainment industry, mother-career synergy, intense effort.

MOON_IN_11.name: Moon in 11th: Lābha-Mano Yoga. Continuous wealth, friend/heart-fame per Phaladeepika 8.
MOON_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Moon in the 11th forms a Lābha-Mano Yoga — continuous wealth gains, friend/family-driven emotional fulfilment, elder-sibling support, and steady desire-fulfilment. BPHS Ch.22 — Moon in the gain-bhava augments all life-domains. Common in those whose income flows from public goodwill or social network.
MOON_IN_11.general: Lābha-Mano Yoga, continuous wealth, friend/heart-fame, elder-sibling support, desire-fulfilment.

MOON_IN_12.name: Moon in 12th: spends freely, loves solitude, rich dream-life, mokṣa-leaning per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
MOON_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Moon in the 12th makes the native free-spending, fond of solitude, rich in sleep and dreams, and inclined to foreign residence. BPHS Ch.22 — the Moon in the vyaya-bhava turns the mind inward and imaginative with heavy expenditure, yet it inclines toward liberation-practice, bed-comforts, and deep imagination — a poet/artist-maker placement. A weak (dark) Moon here magnifies anxiety and mental restlessness.
MOON_IN_12.general: Free spending, love of solitude, imaginative mind, mokṣa-leaning, foreign residence.

MOON_IN_2.name: Moon in 2nd: sweet speech, savings, family affection, love of food per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
MOON_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Moon in the 2nd grants sweet speech, a saving disposition, family affection, and love of fine food and tastes. BPHS Ch.22 — a strong (waxing/well-placed) Moon in the wealth-bhava brings prosperity; a weak Moon makes wealth fluctuating like the tides. The mind’s softness surfaces through the voice; the family bond is warm.
MOON_IN_2.general: Sweet speech, savings, family affection, love of food, wealth steady-or-fluctuating by Moon’s strength.

MOON_IN_3.name: Moon in 3rd: sibling happiness, courage, fond of travel, restless mind per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
MOON_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Moon in the 3rd grants sibling happiness (especially sisters), courage, fondness for travel, and a restless, mobile mind. BPHS Ch.22 — the Moon in this upachaya strengthens initiative, communication and artistic skill, and brings many friends. The mind’s enthusiasm expresses itself through enterprise and short journeys.
MOON_IN_3.general: Sibling happiness, courage, love of travel, restless mind, communication skill.

MOON_IN_4.name: Moon in 4th: dig-balī Mātṛ-Gṛha Raja Yoga. Profound maternal happiness, heart-peace per Phaladeepika 8.
MOON_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Moon in the 4th forms a dig-balī Mātṛ-Gṛha Raja Yoga — the Moon (kāraka of mother + heart) is directionally exalted in the comfort-bhava itself. The native enjoys profound maternal happiness, domestic peace, heart-contentment, and dharmic householder life. BPHS Ch.22 — the Moon's 4th-house placement is its supreme directional strength. Signature of those rooted in family and home.
MOON_IN_4.general: Dig-balī Mātṛ-Gṛha Raja Yoga, profound maternal happiness, heart-peace, domestic prosperity, dharmic householder.

MOON_IN_5.name: Moon in 5th: Mano-Prajñā Raja Yoga (kāraka-trikoṇa). Intellect, progeny, mantra skill per Phaladeepika 8.
MOON_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Moon in the 5th forms a Mano-Prajñā Raja Yoga — the mind-significator in the bhava of past-merit and progeny. The native enjoys intuitive intellect, progeny happiness, mantra-skill, and fame for emotional intelligence. BPHS Ch.22 — kāraka-trikoṇa Raja-yoga. Common in poets, devotional musicians, and spiritually-attuned counselors.
MOON_IN_5.general: Mano-Prajñā Raja Yoga, intuitive intellect, progeny, mantra skill, emotional-intelligence fame.

MOON_IN_6.name: Moon in 6th: emotional unrest, stomach ailments, debt/enemy worry, service-leaning per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
MOON_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Moon in the 6th tends toward emotional unrest, stomach/water-related ailments, worry over debts and enemies, and a service disposition. BPHS Ch.22 — the Moon in the foe-bhava suffers a kāraka loss (the mind placed in a dusthāna), bringing mental instability and concern for the mother’s health. Yet being an upachaya it also grants victory over enemies and standing in service/healthcare fields. Strength of the Moon decides which side prevails.
MOON_IN_6.general: Emotional unrest, stomach ailments, debt/enemy worry, service-leaning, mother’s health concern.

MOON_IN_7.name: Moon in 7th: emotionally-rich spousal yoga. Gentle spouse, gainful travel, empathetic disposition per Phaladeepika 8.
MOON_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Moon in the 7th forms an emotionally-rich spousal yoga — gentle spouse, gainful travel, cooperative business, and natural counsellor-quality. BPHS Ch.22 — Moon in kalatra-bhava produces empathetic interpersonal style. Common in therapists, mediators, and partnership-oriented professionals.
MOON_IN_7.general: Emotional spousal yoga, gentle spouse, gainful travel, cooperative business, counsellor temperament.

MOON_IN_8.name: Moon in 8th: emotional fragility, mother’s health concern, drawn to occult per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
MOON_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Moon in the 8th tends toward emotional fragility, depressive moods, concern for the mother’s longevity, and water-related ailments. BPHS Ch.22 — the Moon in the randhra-bhava unsettles the mind and inclines toward fear, yet it also draws the native to the occult, tantra, astrology, and the search into life’s depths and longevity. A full (bright) Moon with benefic aspect materially heals the affliction.
MOON_IN_8.general: Emotional fragility, depressive moods, mother’s health concern, occult interest, water ailments.

MOON_IN_9.name: Moon in 9th: fortunate, dharmic, fond of pilgrimage, devoted heart per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
MOON_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Moon in the 9th makes the native fortunate, religious, fond of pilgrimage, devoted to the guru, and dharmically attached to the mother. BPHS Ch.22 — the Moon in the fortune-trine is benefic, giving the mind a dharmic bent, popular appeal, gainful travel, and goodwill. A full (bright) Moon makes the rise of fortune clear and well-timed.
MOON_IN_9.general: Rise of fortune, dharmic disposition, pilgrimage, popular appeal, devotion to guru.

RAHU_IN_1.name: Rahu in 1st: intense ambition, unconventional persona, illusory pull, ego-confusion per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_1.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in Lagna makes the native intensely ambitious, with an unconventional and magnetic persona and a taste for foreign/unusual subjects, yet prone to illusion and ego-inflation. Rahu in the body-bhava heightens the urge for self-display, brings sudden rises and falls, and can affect the skin or head. In a benefic sign or under benefic aspect it yields mass-influence; afflicted, it brings confusion and loss of standing. Its results sharpen in the Rahu daśā.
RAHU_IN_1.general: Intense ambition, unconventional persona, foreign attraction, illusory tendencies, sudden rise.

RAHU_IN_10.name: Rahu in 10th: unconventional Karma Raja Yoga. Foreign-business fame, sudden authority per BPHS 28.
RAHU_IN_10.prose: Per BPHS Ch.28, Rahu in the 10th forms an unconventional Karma Raja Yoga — fame through foreign business, sudden authority, abrupt rise to high office, and unconventional career fame. Phaladeepika Ch.8 — Rahu's 10th-house placement is exceptionally auspicious. Common in tech entrepreneurs, foreign-investment professionals, and those whose career path is non-traditional.
RAHU_IN_10.general: Unconventional Karma Raja Yoga, foreign-business fame, sudden authority, abrupt rise, non-traditional career.

RAHU_IN_11.name: Rahu in 11th: unconventional Lābha Yoga. Wealth via foreign sources, sudden desire-fulfilment per BPHS 28.
RAHU_IN_11.prose: Per BPHS Ch.28, Rahu in the 11th forms an unconventional Lābha Yoga — wealth via foreign sources, sudden/unexpected desire-fulfilment, and friend-family expansion. Phaladeepika Ch.8 — Rahu's 11th-house placement is exceptionally auspicious. Common in cross-border traders, NRI-business operators, and those whose income pathway is non-traditional.
RAHU_IN_11.general: Unconventional Lābha Yoga, foreign wealth, sudden desire-fulfilment, friend-family expansion, non-traditional gains.

RAHU_IN_12.name: Rahu in 12th: foreign-residence yoga, heavy expenditure, covert work, mokṣa/illusion duality per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_12.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 12th gives a strong yoga for foreign residence, heavy expenditure, skill in covert work, but a proneness to insomnia, illusion, and hidden enemies. Rahu in the vyaya-bhava creates a tug between liberation and māyā, with expenditure (and gains) linked to foreign lands and a pull toward secret research/tantra. Under benefic aspect it gives stable settlement abroad and a spiritual yoga; afflicted, insomnia, fear, and draining losses.
RAHU_IN_12.general: Foreign-residence yoga, heavy expenditure, covert work, mokṣa/illusion duality, insomnia.

RAHU_IN_2.name: Rahu in 2nd: wealth from unconventional sources, erratic speech, foreign income per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_2.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 2nd gives wealth from unconventional sources, foreign or technology-based income, but erratic speech and a pull toward associations outside the family. Rahu in the wealth-bhava brings fluctuating finances, sudden gains and losses, and possible mouth/dietary issues. Under benefic aspect it can amass great wealth through unusual trade; afflicted, it inclines toward false speech and family disputes over money.
RAHU_IN_2.general: Unconventional wealth, erratic speech, foreign income, financial fluctuation, sudden gain/loss.

RAHU_IN_3.name: Rahu in 3rd: extraordinary-courage yoga. Foreign travel, sudden fame, sibling power per BPHS 28.
RAHU_IN_3.prose: Per BPHS Ch.28, Rahu in the 3rd forms an extraordinary-courage yoga — outsized boldness, elder-sibling power, foreign travel, and sudden/unconventional fame. Phaladeepika Ch.8 — Rahu in upachaya bhavas (3/6/10/11) yields its best fruit, mirroring Saturn. Common in expatriates, adventurers, and breakthrough entrepreneurs.
RAHU_IN_3.general: Extraordinary-courage yoga, sudden fame, foreign travel, sibling power, unconventional drive.

RAHU_IN_4.name: Rahu in 4th: domestic unrest, separation from mother, foreign-home yoga, mental restlessness per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_4.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 4th tends toward domestic unrest, reduced maternal comfort or separation from the mother, a yoga for living abroad, and mental restlessness. Rahu in the comfort-bhava brings uncertainty over property/vehicles, frequent relocation, and an unconventional home environment. Under benefic aspect it can give gains through foreign land/property; afflicted, it brings home discord and an unsettled mind.
RAHU_IN_4.general: Domestic unrest, separation from mother, foreign-home yoga, mental restlessness, relocation.

RAHU_IN_5.name: Rahu in 5th: unconventional intellect, progeny concern, occult/speculative leaning per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_5.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 5th gives an unconventional, sharp intellect, courage in speculation/stocks, a pull toward mantra/tantra/occult knowledge, but concern or delay regarding children. Rahu in the progeny-bhava signals unusual past-karma patterns and possible difficulty with conception. Under benefic aspect it yields a technical-genius/wealth yoga; afflicted, it brings progeny difficulty and a risk of addictive speculation.
RAHU_IN_5.general: Unconventional intellect, speculative courage, occult leaning, progeny concern, technical genius.

RAHU_IN_6.name: Rahu in 6th: enemy-destruction Vipareeta-Raja Yoga. Defeats powerful foes, debt-cancellation per BPHS 28.
RAHU_IN_6.prose: Per BPHS Ch.28, Rahu in the 6th forms an enemy-destruction Vipareeta-Raja Yoga — Rahu in dusthana cancels debt, defeats powerful enemies (legal/political adversaries), and confers unconventional power and authority-fame. Phaladeepika Ch.8 — Rahu's 6th-house placement is among the most auspicious for the shadow planet. Common in litigators, adversarial-arena professionals.
RAHU_IN_6.general: Enemy-destruction Vipareeta-Raja Yoga, victory over powerful foes, debt-cancellation, unconventional power, authority-fame.

RAHU_IN_7.name: Rahu in 7th: unconventional marriage, foreign partner, fluctuating business, relationship illusion per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_7.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 7th indicates an unconventional or foreign spousal connection, illusion/uncertainty in marriage, and fluctuating business. Rahu in the partnership-bhava brings a cross-cultural or unusual partner and sudden shifts in partnerships. Under benefic aspect it gives a foreign-partnership/business yoga; afflicted, it brings marital confusion and fear of separation. Mature, clear-eyed commitment is the corrective.
RAHU_IN_7.general: Unconventional marriage, foreign partner, fluctuating business, relationship illusion, partnership shifts.

RAHU_IN_8.name: Rahu in 8th: occult/tantric power, sudden events, hidden gains, longevity concern per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_8.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 8th gives power in occult/tantra/astrology research, a proneness to sudden events, hidden or inheritance-based gains, but concern over longevity and health. Rahu in the randhra-bhava brings abrupt rises and falls, attraction to secret knowledge, and deep-seated psychological fears. Under benefic aspect it forms a research-tantra-wealth yoga; afflicted, it raises the risk of accidents and hidden enemies.
RAHU_IN_8.general: Occult/tantric power, sudden events, hidden gains, longevity concern, attraction to secrets.

RAHU_IN_9.name: Rahu in 9th: unconventional faith, fortune via foreign lands, friction with guru, philosophical inquiry per BPHS.
RAHU_IN_9.prose: Per BPHS, Rahu in the 9th makes the native an inquirer into unconventional religion/philosophy, fortunate through foreign lands, but prone to friction with traditional guru-figures. Rahu in the fortune-trine brings unusual worldviews, long-distance travel yogas, and doubt/illusion regarding the father or preceptor. Under benefic aspect it gives fame through foreign philosophy/study; afflicted, it brings doctrinal confusion and difficulty for the father.
RAHU_IN_9.general: Unconventional faith, fortune via foreign lands, friction with guru, philosophical inquiry, long travel.

SATURN_IN_1.name: Saturn in 1st: slow start, serious, hardworking, delayed rise, Vāta ailments per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in Lagna makes the native serious, hardworking, reserved in speech, and slow to start, yet patient and enduring. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn in the body-bhava brings childhood hardship, a delayed rise, and Vāta-type ailments, but grants stable standing and diligence in the latter half of life. When Saturn is exalted/own-sign, it gives sober, durable leadership; when afflicted, a long struggle precedes success.
SATURN_IN_1.general: Seriousness, diligence, delayed rise, Vāta ailments, stability in later life.

SATURN_IN_10.name: Saturn in 10th: dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga (Śaśa-flavour). Long-haul fame, royal honour per Phaladeepika 8.
SATURN_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 10th forms a special Karma Raja Yoga — Saturn in the career-bhava is dig-balī (directionally strong), conferring long-haul career fame, royal recognition, service-leadership, and stable high office. BPHS Ch.25 — dig-balī Saturn augments career fame. Mirror of (but distinct from) Śaśa Mahāpurusha; native's work outlasts contemporaries.
SATURN_IN_10.general: Dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga, long-haul fame, royal recognition, service-leadership, stable high office.

SATURN_IN_11.name: Saturn in 11th: Lābha-Sthairya Yoga. Long-term wealth accumulation, service-class fame per Phaladeepika 8.
SATURN_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 11th forms a Lābha-Sthairya Yoga — long-term wealth accumulation, fame within the service/working class, and stable desire-fulfilment. BPHS Ch.25 — the 11th is Saturn's most exalted house, conferring sustained gains. The signature placement for those who build slowly but become reliably wealthy in old age.
SATURN_IN_11.general: Lābha-Sthairya Yoga, long-term wealth, service-class fame, stable desire-fulfilment, retirement prosperity.

SATURN_IN_12.name: Saturn in 12th: controlled expenditure, solitary detachment, foreign residence, mokṣa-leaning per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 12th makes the native expense-prone yet self-restrained, inclined to solitary detachment, fond of foreign residence, and skilled in behind-the-scenes work. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn as the significator of liberation in the vyaya-bhava supports renunciation, yoga-discipline, and work linked to hidden service, prisons, or ashrams. When afflicted it gives insomnia and hidden enemies; with benefic aspect, a mokṣa/tapas yoga and stable work abroad.
SATURN_IN_12.general: Controlled expenditure, solitary detachment, foreign residence, mokṣa-leaning, behind-the-scenes skill.

SATURN_IN_2.name: Saturn in 2nd: delayed savings, measured speech, wealth by toil, family burden per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 2nd gives measured or blunt speech, wealth earned through toil, delayed savings, and the carrying of family burdens. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn in the wealth-bhava brings early financial hardship but, through perseverance and thrift, builds stable accumulation later in life. When afflicted it concerns the eyes/teeth; when exalted it amasses great wealth through sustained labour.
SATURN_IN_2.general: Measured speech, wealth by toil, delayed savings, family burden, late-life accumulation.

SATURN_IN_3.name: Saturn in 3rd: Dhairya-Parākrama Yoga. Fame via long effort, sibling longevity per Phaladeepika 8.
SATURN_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 3rd forms a Dhairya-Parākrama Yoga — fame through long-haul effort, elder-sibling longevity, and stable enterprise. BPHS Ch.25 — Saturn in upachaya bhavas (3/6/10/11) is auspicious; it builds slowly but unshakably. Common in marathon-career professionals and patient entrepreneurs.
SATURN_IN_3.general: Dhairya-Parākrama Yoga, fame via long effort, elder-sibling longevity, stable enterprise.

SATURN_IN_4.name: Saturn in 4th: reduced home comfort, mother’s difficulty, inner discontent per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 4th tends to reduce home comfort, bring difficulty to the mother, inner discontent, and a tendency to leave the birthplace. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn works against the kāraka grain here (it opposes the comfort-significator Moon), lowering domestic peace and sometimes giving early maternal separation. Yet land, mining, and antique/old-property business build stable assets later. Benefic aspect softens the affliction.
SATURN_IN_4.general: Reduced home comfort, mother’s difficulty, inner discontent, leaving birthplace, late property gains.

SATURN_IN_5.name: Saturn in 5th: delayed progeny, deep mind, disciplined practice, anxious streak per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 5th gives a deep, far-sighted mind but tends toward delayed or few children and an anxious disposition. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn in the progeny-bhava delays the fruits of past merit and disturbs the significator of offspring, yet grants profound research-intellect and disciplined mantra practice. With benefic aspect, progeny-happiness comes after delay; an exalted Saturn gives long-range strategic wisdom.
SATURN_IN_5.general: Delayed progeny, deep mind, disciplined practice, anxious streak, far-sighted strategy.

SATURN_IN_6.name: Saturn in 6th: enemy-disease-victory yoga. Long-struggle triumph, service-fame per Phaladeepika 8.
SATURN_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 6th forms an enemy-disease-victory Vipareeta-style yoga — long-struggle triumph over enemies, recovery from chronic disease, debt-cancellation, and fame for service. BPHS Ch.25 — Saturn in upachaya yields its best fruit. Common in those whose careers are built on overcoming sustained adversity.
SATURN_IN_6.general: Enemy-disease-victory yoga, long-struggle triumph, debt-cancellation, service-fame, perseverance.

SATURN_IN_7.name: Saturn in 7th: delayed marriage, stable union, older/serious partner, steady in business per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 7th indicates delayed marriage but a long, stable union, an older or serious-minded partner, and patient skill in business/partnership. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn in the partnership-bhava brings early coolness in relationships but loyalty and durable partnership-stability later. When exalted/own-sign it gives an enduring marriage; when afflicted, marital coldness or fear of separation. Maturity and patience are the corrective.
SATURN_IN_7.general: Delayed marriage, stable union, older/serious partner, business patience, durable partnership.

SATURN_IN_8.name: Saturn in 8th: longevity yoga, deep research, frail health, delayed inheritance per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 8th makes the native long-lived and inclined to occult research, though prone to frail health and Vāta ailments. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn as the significator of longevity in the longevity-bhava (kāraka in its own house) grants a long life, yet brings chronic/lingering illness, delayed inheritance/legacy gains, and concern over hidden enemies. With benefic aspect it forms a deep-research-and-longevity yoga.
SATURN_IN_8.general: Longevity, deep research, frail health, delayed inheritance, Vāta ailments.

SATURN_IN_9.name: Saturn in 9th: delayed fortune, father’s difficulty, dharmic discipline, justice-loving per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 24.
SATURN_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Saturn in the 9th makes the native dutiful in dharma, justice-loving, and fortunate through hard effort, but with delayed fortune and a tendency to difficulty regarding the father. BPHS Ch.24 — Saturn in the fortune-trine delays the fruits of past merit and lowers paternal comfort, yet through severe labour and adherence to justice it grants stable fortune and dharmic standing later. An exalted Saturn gives leadership in law/justice.
SATURN_IN_9.general: Delayed fortune, father’s difficulty, dharmic discipline, love of justice, fortune via effort.

SUN_IN_1.name: Sun in Lagna: lustrous, self-respecting, pitta-natured, royal honour per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Sun in Lagna confers lustrous appearance, self-respect, pitta-natured constitution, fierce temperament, and royal recognition. BPHS Ch.21 — the soul-significator in the body-bhava augments self-radiance but slightly diminishes paternal happiness (since Sun aspects 7th, leaving 9th un-aspected). Common in leaders, executives, and those whose personality itself is the engine of authority.
SUN_IN_1.general: Lustrous appearance, self-respect, royal recognition, fierce temperament, pitta-natured constitution.

SUN_IN_10.name: Sun in 10th: dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga. High office, authority, royal honour, stable fame per Phaladeepika 8.
SUN_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Sun in the 10th forms a dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga — Sun in karma-bhava is directionally exalted. The native attains high office, exercises real authority, receives royal recognition, and earns stable fame. BPHS Ch.21 — the 10th is the Sun's most exalted house. Co-forms Amala Yoga (benefic in 10th from Lagna or Moon). Signature placement of statesmen and CEOs.
SUN_IN_10.general: Dig-balī Karma Raja Yoga, high office, authority, royal recognition, stable fame, Amala-quality reputation.

SUN_IN_11.name: Sun in 11th: Rāja-Lābha Yoga. Wealth via royal recognition, elder-sibling power per Phaladeepika 8.
SUN_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Sun in the 11th forms a Rāja-Lābha Yoga — wealth via royal recognition, powerful elder siblings, authority-driven fame, and steady desire-fulfilment. BPHS Ch.21 — Sun in the upachaya-gain bhava augments all life-domains. Common in those whose income flows from holding office or executive recognition.
SUN_IN_11.general: Rāja-Lābha Yoga, royal-recognition wealth, elder-sibling power, authority fame, desire-fulfilment.

SUN_IN_12.name: Sun in 12th: heavy expenditure, separation from father, eye trouble, mokṣa-leaning per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 12th tends toward heavy expenditure, reduced paternal comfort, eye trouble, or loss of standing. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun in the vyaya-bhava spends its radiance, with possible friction with authority and a pull toward foreign residence. Yet the same placement can incline toward liberation, solitary practice, and worthwhile spiritual expenditure. With benefic aspect it can yield fame earned abroad.
SUN_IN_12.general: Heavy expenditure, separation from father, eye trouble, foreign residence, mokṣa-leaning.

SUN_IN_2.name: Sun in 2nd: harsh speech, family discord, strained eyes/wealth, gains via authority per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 2nd produces harsh or commanding speech, wealth earned through government/authority, but a tendency to pride-driven friction within the family. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun in the wealth-bhava signals possible eye strain, mouth/dental issues, and ego-born family discord, even as state-service brings income. The dignity of the Sun and aspects to the 2nd decide whether the wealth or the friction dominates.
SUN_IN_2.general: Harsh speech, authority-driven wealth, family friction, eye/dental sensitivity, pride.

SUN_IN_3.name: Sun in 3rd: Parākrama Yoga. Courage, self-made victory, eminence among siblings per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 3rd (an upachaya) confers valour, courage, and victory through self-effort, with limited sibling comfort yet eminence over them. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun in the prowess-bhava strengthens initiative, industriousness, and the dispelling of enemies. A constructive placement: the Sun grows in upachaya houses, so its fruits rise over time.
SUN_IN_3.general: Valour, courage, self-made victory, eminence among siblings, industriousness.

SUN_IN_4.name: Sun in 4th: reduced maternal comfort, domestic unrest, inner heat per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 4th tends to reduce maternal comfort, bring domestic unrest, and create inner restlessness — the comfort-bhava itself is weakened. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun here sits against the kāraka grain (it opposes the comfort-significator Moon), so home/vehicle ease diminishes and the mother’s health may concern. Yet paternal status or an inherited position can still elevate the native. The Sun’s dignity decides how heavily the friction lands.
SUN_IN_4.general: Reduced maternal comfort, domestic unrest, inner heat, less ease, possible inherited status.

SUN_IN_5.name: Sun in 5th: sharp intellect, few/late progeny, royal favour, higher learning per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 5th grants sharp intellect, skill in mantra/learning, and royal favour, but tends toward few children or delayed progeny. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun in the progeny-bhava confers brilliance of mind and father-linked fame, yet as a weak significator of children it asks effort for offspring. Strong dignity turns the intellect toward authority and statecraft; affliction concentrates the progeny difficulty.
SUN_IN_5.general: Sharp intellect, higher learning, royal favour, few children, delayed progeny.

SUN_IN_6.name: Sun in 6th: conqueror of enemies, disease-destroyer, strong, debt-free per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 6th makes the native a conqueror of enemies, a destroyer of disease, strong, and free of debt. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun is powerful in this upachaya: it shatters the enemy-camp, burns away illness by its own heat, and grants victory in competition and litigation. One of the Sun’s genuinely favourable placements, its fruits strengthening with age.
SUN_IN_6.general: Victory over enemies, disease destroyed, strength, freedom from debt, competitive success.

SUN_IN_7.name: Sun in 7th: marital friction, delayed marriage, fame via authority per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 7th tends toward marital friction, ego-clashes with the partner, or delayed marriage. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun as ego-significator in the partnership-bhava strains domestic harmony, though state-service or business brings fame. An aspect from Venus (kāraka of marriage) softens the affliction; a strong, well-dignified Sun shifts the energy toward a dignified, authoritative spouse rather than discord.
SUN_IN_7.general: Marital friction, delayed marriage, independent partner, fame via authority, ego-clashes.

SUN_IN_8.name: Sun in 8th: weakened eye-vitality, father’s difficulty, health concern, muted fame per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 21.
SUN_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, the Sun in the 8th tends to weaken eye-vitality, bring difficulty to the father, sudden health concerns, and muted public fame. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun in the randhra-bhava suffers a loss of its natural radiance, with possible afflictions to the father’s longevity and to the native’s standing. Lifespan itself can be long, but recognition demands sustained effort. Benefic aspects materially soften the placement.
SUN_IN_8.general: Weakened eye-vitality, father’s difficulty, health concern, loss of standing, muted fame.

SUN_IN_9.name: Sun in 9th: Pitṛ-Bhāgya Yoga. Paternal happiness, dharma, royal fame, guru-grace per Phaladeepika 8.
SUN_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Sun in the 9th forms a Pitṛ-Bhāgya Yoga — paternal happiness, dharmic disposition, royal fame, and guru-grace. BPHS Ch.21 — the Sun (kāraka of father) in the bhāgya-bhava forms a kāraka-trikoṇa Raja-yoga structure. Common in those whose father is a positive force in their life and whose dharmic standing is recognized.
SUN_IN_9.general: Pitṛ-Bhāgya Yoga, paternal happiness, dharmic disposition, royal fame, guru's grace.

VENUS_IN_1.name: Venus in Lagna: beautiful form, art-loving, sensory abundance, charm per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_1.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in Lagna confers physical beauty, art-loving disposition, sensory abundance, contentment, and respect from women. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus in the body-bhava grants an artistic, refined personality. Common in performers, designers, and those whose careers leverage charm and aesthetics.
VENUS_IN_1.general: Beauty, artistic temperament, sensory abundance, respect from women, refined manners.

VENUS_IN_10.name: Venus in 10th: fame through art/career. Beauty-luxury profession, sweet renown per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_10.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 10th confers fame through art and career — recognition in beauty, arts, luxury, fashion, jewellery, and entertainment, with sweet renown and royal honour. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus in the karma-kendra (near its directional strength) builds reputation through an aesthetic profession. Career often grows through women’s support or partnership. Signature placement of artists, designers, and luxury entrepreneurs.
VENUS_IN_10.general: Fame via art/career, beauty-luxury profession, sweet renown, royal honour, partnership-driven career.

VENUS_IN_11.name: Venus in 11th: Lābha-Kalā Yoga. Continuous gains, wealth via women/friends per Phaladeepika 8.
VENUS_IN_11.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 11th forms a Lābha-Kalā Yoga — continuous wealth gains, women/friend-driven income, fame through artistic ventures, and steady desire-fulfilment. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus in the gain-bhava augments all life-domains. Common in entertainment-industry professionals and those whose income flows from aesthetic enterprises.
VENUS_IN_11.general: Lābha-Kalā Yoga, continuous gains, women/friend wealth, artistic ventures, desire-fulfilment.

VENUS_IN_12.name: Venus in 12th: Śayyā-Sukha (bed-comfort) Yoga, sensory spending, mokṣa-art leaning per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_12.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 12th makes the native rich in bed-comforts, free-spending on luxury/pleasure, fond of foreign residence, and inclined to private romance. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus is a significator of expenditure in the vyaya-bhava, yet it gives excellent results in bed-pleasures (the pleasure-kāraka in the comfort-of-bed house) and a leaning toward liberation-art — this is the famed "Śayyā-Sukha Yoga." Control of luxury-spending is nonetheless needed.
VENUS_IN_12.general: Śayyā-Sukha Yoga, sensory/luxury spending, foreign residence, mokṣa-art leaning, private romance.

VENUS_IN_2.name: Venus in 2nd: Dhana-Kalā Yoga. Sweet speech, fine possessions, family comfort per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_2.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 2nd forms a Dhana-Kalā Yoga — sweet speech, wealth, a collection of beautiful objects and jewellery, and family comfort. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus in the wealth-bhava generates income through art/luxury trade and a pleasing manner of speaking. Wealth often grows through women or partnerships. Common in those dealing in beauty, fashion, jewellery, and the fine arts.
VENUS_IN_2.general: Dhana-Kalā Yoga, sweet speech, fine possessions, family comfort, art/luxury income.

VENUS_IN_3.name: Venus in 3rd: artistic communication skill, sister happiness, fond of pleasant travel per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_3.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 3rd grants artistic and communicative skill, happiness through sisters, fondness for comfortable travel, and a pleasant manner. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus in this upachaya gives prowess in art/dance/music, comfort through friends, and skill in promoting beauty/aesthetics. Its own kāraka gifts dim slightly, but the upachaya nature builds the fruits over time. Common in performers, media/PR, and creative communicators.
VENUS_IN_3.general: Artistic communication, sister happiness, pleasant travel, charming manner, comfort via friends.

VENUS_IN_4.name: Venus in 4th: home/vehicle/sensory abundance, maternal happiness per Phaladeepika 8.
VENUS_IN_4.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 4th confers home/vehicle/sensory abundance, beautiful domestic life, maternal happiness, and wealth augmented through women's cooperation. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus in the comfort-bhava forms a sensory-kendra Raja-yoga. Common in interior designers, hospitality professionals, and those whose home itself is the source of fortune.
VENUS_IN_4.general: Home/vehicle/sensory abundance, maternal happiness, beautiful home, women-driven wealth, heart-pleasure.

VENUS_IN_5.name: Venus in 5th: poetry-art-progeny Raja Yoga. Intellect, artistry, progeny per Phaladeepika 8.
VENUS_IN_5.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 5th forms a poetry-art-progeny Raja Yoga — intellect, artistic disposition, progeny happiness, romantic relationships, and royal fame. BPHS Ch.22 — kāraka-trikoṇa Raja-yoga. Signature placement in poets, artists, dancers, and those whose creativity itself is their fortune.
VENUS_IN_5.general: Poetry-art-progeny Raja Yoga, intellect, artistry, progeny, romantic relationships, royal fame.

VENUS_IN_6.name: Venus in 6th: reduced marital comfort, pleasure-obstacles, service/art livelihood per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_6.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 6th tends to reduce marital comfort, obstruct pleasures, or bring relationship friction, yet grants proficiency in service/art/healthcare fields. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus suffers a kāraka-loss here (the marriage-significator afflicted in a dusthāna), straining the partnership and raising the chance of debt/disputes. Being an upachaya, it also gives victory over enemies and a livelihood through art or service.
VENUS_IN_6.general: Reduced marital comfort, pleasure-obstacles, service/art livelihood, debt/disputes, victory over enemies.

VENUS_IN_7.name: Venus in 7th: kāraka-kāraka spousal yoga. Beautiful spouse, marital harmony per Phaladeepika 8.
VENUS_IN_7.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 7th forms a kāraka-kāraka spousal yoga — Venus (kāraka of relationship) in kalatra-bhava itself. The native enjoys a beautiful spouse, marital harmony, and elevation through women's cooperation. BPHS Ch.22 — the supreme spousal placement. Common in those whose marriage itself is their fortune-generator.
VENUS_IN_7.general: Beautiful spouse, marital harmony, women-driven elevation, business profits, gainful travel.

VENUS_IN_8.name: Venus in 8th: inheritance/spousal wealth, hidden pleasures, but spouse-longevity concern per Phaladeepika 8 / BPHS 22.
VENUS_IN_8.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 8th grants gains through inheritance/legacy, a taste for hidden pleasures, and enduring sensory capacity, but raises concern over the spouse’s longevity or secrecy in relationships. BPHS Ch.22 — Venus suffers a disturbance of its marriage-significance in the randhra-bhava, yet brings sudden wealth, spouse-linked or in-law wealth, and a pull toward the esoteric/hidden arts. Benefic aspect yields a legacy/inheritance yoga.
VENUS_IN_8.general: Inheritance/spousal wealth, hidden pleasures, sudden gains, spouse-longevity concern, enduring sensuality.

VENUS_IN_9.name: Venus in 9th: kāraka-trikoṇa Raja Yoga. Dharmic artist, fortune via women per Phaladeepika 8.
VENUS_IN_9.prose: Per Phaladeepika Ch.8, Venus in the 9th forms a kāraka-trikoṇa Raja Yoga — dharmic artist, fortune-elevation through women, gainful religious travel, and guru-grace mediated through aesthetic/devotional channels. BPHS Ch.22 — fortune-bhava + Venus = devotional artistry. Common in temple musicians, sacred artists, and those whose dharmic life is mediated through beauty.
VENUS_IN_9.general: Bhāgya-Kalā Raja Yoga, dharmic artist, women-driven fortune, religious travel, guru's grace.

AQUARIUS.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Aquarius, the Ishta-devata is Saturn / Shiva.
AQUARIUS.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Aquarius, the Ishta-devata is generally Shani or Shiva; worship granting detachment, service, wisdom and liberation is commended.
AQUARIUS.lagnaPhala: Aquarius Lagna: reflective, humanitarian, independent-minded, serious. Saturnine far-sightedness (Brihat Jataka 1).
AQUARIUS.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Reflectiveness, humanitarianism, independence, foresight, friendship, stubbornness, tall physique.
AQUARIUS.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, an Aquarius ascendant gives a tall-to-medium build, a serious face, a reflective mind, humanitarian concern, an independent outlook, and a love of friends. Saturn’s rulership grants foresight, endurance, and social-mindedness; aloofness and stubbornness are the flaws. Saravali calls this air-fixed sign a reformer and deep thinker, drawn to collective welfare and unconventional causes.

ARIES.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Aries, the Ishta-devata is the Sun / Kartikeya.
ARIES.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Aries, the Ishta-devata is generally the Sun or Kartikeya; worship granting vigour, strength and courage is commended.
ARIES.lagnaPhala: Aries Lagna: bold, independent, pioneering, restless. Lean energetic frame, quick temper, natural leader (Brihat Jataka 1).
ARIES.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Courage, leadership, independence, fast decisions, competitiveness, impulsive temper, lean energetic physique.
ARIES.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, an Aries ascendant gives a lean-to-medium build, ruddy-fair complexion, restless eyes, courage, a fiery temperament, and an independent, leadership-seeking nature. Mars’ rulership grants self-drive, competitiveness, and rapid decision-making; anger and impulsiveness are the standing flaws. Saravali Ch.5 notes this fire-movable sign produces enterprising, forward-charging, combat-ready natives who lead from the front but tire of routine.

CANCER.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Cancer, the Ishta-devata is Parvati / the Moon.
CANCER.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Cancer, the Ishta-devata is generally Parvati or Chandra; worship granting peace of mind, maternal comfort and emotional stability is commended.
CANCER.lagnaPhala: Cancer Lagna: emotional, family-devoted, home-loving, sensitive. Lunar changeability of mood (Brihat Jataka 1).
CANCER.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Emotional depth, family devotion, sensitivity, memory, imagination, moodiness, fair physique.
CANCER.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Cancer ascendant gives a stout-to-medium build, fair complexion, a tender heart, attachment to mother, home, and water, sensitivity, and a vivid imagination. The Moon’s rulership grants emotional depth, strong memory, and a nurturing instinct; moodiness and over-sensitivity are the flaws. Saravali calls this water-movable sign changeable, affection-led, and drawn to caring and public service.

CAPRICORN.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Capricorn, the Ishta-devata is Saturn / Krishna.
CAPRICORN.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Capricorn, the Ishta-devata is generally Shani or Krishna; worship granting patience, work, justice and Saturn’s peace is commended.
CAPRICORN.lagnaPhala: Capricorn Lagna: duty-bound, patient, ambitious, serious. Saturnine capacity for sustained toil (Brihat Jataka 1).
CAPRICORN.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Duty, patience, ambition, industriousness, endurance, over-worry, lean physique.
CAPRICORN.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Capricorn ascendant gives a lean, tallish build, a serious face, a sense of duty, patience, ambition, and practical competence. Saturn’s rulership grants industriousness, endurance, and long-range vision; over-worry and pessimism are the flaws. Saravali calls this earth-movable sign enterprising, a step-by-step climber who prospers in the latter half of life through persistence.

GEMINI.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Gemini, the Ishta-devata is Vishnu / Saraswati.
GEMINI.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Gemini, the Ishta-devata is generally Vishnu or Saraswati; worship granting intellect, learning and eloquence is commended.
GEMINI.lagnaPhala: Gemini Lagna: intelligent, articulate, restless-minded, dual-natured. Mercurial skill in communication (Brihat Jataka 1).
GEMINI.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Intellect, communication skill, reasoning, multi-tasking, wit, mental restlessness, slender frame.
GEMINI.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Gemini ascendant gives a medium, slender build, lively eyes, eloquence, sharp intellect, wit, and a dual-natured, adaptable mind. Mercury’s rulership grants reasoning, conversational skill, and the capacity to absorb many subjects; restlessness and indecision are the flaws. Saravali calls this air-dual sign skilled in writing, commerce, and communication — versatile, curious, and quick, though scattered if undisciplined.

LEO.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Leo, the Ishta-devata is Shiva / the Sun.
LEO.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Leo, the Ishta-devata is generally Shiva or the Sun; worship granting self-strength, leadership and radiance is commended.
LEO.lagnaPhala: Leo Lagna: radiant, proud, leadership-driven, generous. Solar regality of bearing (Brihat Jataka 1).
LEO.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Radiance, pride, leadership, generosity, firm resolve, ego, tall well-built physique.
LEO.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Leo ascendant gives a tall, well-built frame, a radiant face, pride, a generous heart, a leadership instinct, and firm resolve. The Sun’s rulership grants self-respect, an authoritative bearing, and magnanimity; ego and arrogance are the flaws. Saravali calls this fire-fixed sign kingly, honor-seeking, and sattva-predominant — dignified, commanding, and happiest at the centre.

LIBRA.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Libra, the Ishta-devata is Lakshmi / Saraswati.
LIBRA.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Libra, the Ishta-devata is generally Lakshmi or Saraswati; worship granting balance, fortune, art and justice is commended.
LIBRA.lagnaPhala: Libra Lagna: fair-minded, balanced, art-loving, gracious. Venusian skill with relationships (Brihat Jataka 1).
LIBRA.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Fairness, balance, artistic taste, relational skill, grace, indecision, well-proportioned physique.
LIBRA.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Libra ascendant gives a well-proportioned, tallish build, a pleasant face, a sense of justice, even-handedness, skill in art and dealings, and a love of harmony. Venus’ rulership grants aesthetic taste, balanced judgment, and relational finesse; indecision and procrastination are the flaws. Saravali calls this air-movable sign diplomatic, cooperation-loving, and equilibrium-seeking — the natural mediator.

PISCES.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Pisces, the Ishta-devata is Vishnu / Jupiter.
PISCES.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Pisces, the Ishta-devata is generally Vishnu or Brihaspati; worship granting wisdom, liberation, devotion and compassion is commended.
PISCES.lagnaPhala: Pisces Lagna: emotional, compassionate, spiritual, imaginative. Jupiterian faith and devotion (Brihat Jataka 1).
PISCES.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Emotional depth, compassion, spirituality, imagination, devotion, escapism, soft physique.
PISCES.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Pisces ascendant gives a soft, somewhat full build, gentle eyes, emotional depth, compassion, spirituality, imagination, and devotion. Jupiter’s rulership grants religious faith, a charitable instinct, and inner vision; over-sensitivity and escapism are the flaws. Saravali calls this water-dual sign compassion-led, given to service and renunciation, and naturally inclined toward the spiritual.

SAGITTARIUS.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Sagittarius, the Ishta-devata is Vishnu / Dattatreya.
SAGITTARIUS.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Sagittarius, the Ishta-devata is generally Vishnu or Dattatreya; worship granting wisdom, dharma and the grace of the guru is commended.
SAGITTARIUS.lagnaPhala: Sagittarius Lagna: dharmic, optimistic, frank-spoken, knowledge-loving. Jupiterian principle and ethics (Brihat Jataka 1).
SAGITTARIUS.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Dharma, optimism, love of knowledge, ethics, frank speech, over-optimism, tall well-built physique.
SAGITTARIUS.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Sagittarius ascendant gives a tall, well-built frame, a bright face, religiosity, optimism, plain speech, and a love of knowledge and dharma. Jupiter’s rulership grants ethical conviction, a broad outlook, and a teacher-student spirit; bluntness and over-optimism are the flaws. Saravali calls this fire-dual sign fond of philosophy, pilgrimage, and travel — a preacher and truth-keeper, guided by principle.

SCORPIO.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Scorpio, the Ishta-devata is Narasimha / Hanuman.
SCORPIO.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Scorpio, the Ishta-devata is generally Narasimha or Hanuman; worship granting victory over enemies, courage and protection is commended.
SCORPIO.lagnaPhala: Scorpio Lagna: intense, secretive, iron-willed, drawn to mysteries. Mars-driven indomitable will (Brihat Jataka 1).
SCORPIO.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Will-power, secrecy, fixed resolve, investigation, endurance, jealousy, firm physique.
SCORPIO.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Scorpio ascendant gives a firm, compact, somewhat secretive build, piercing eyes, a deep nature, unbreakable resolve, a love of mysteries, and gravity. Mars’ rulership grants fierce will-power, an investigative drive, and endurance; jealousy and vindictiveness are the flaws. Saravali calls this water-fixed sign a profound researcher, capable of total transformation and drawn to the occult and the hidden.

TAURUS.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Taurus, the Ishta-devata is Gauri / Lakshmi.
TAURUS.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Taurus, the Ishta-devata is generally Gauri or Lakshmi; worship granting fortune, prosperity and grace is commended.
TAURUS.lagnaPhala: Taurus Lagna: steady, patient, comfort- and beauty-loving, attractive. Venusian taste for art and wealth (Brihat Jataka 1).
TAURUS.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Stability, patience, taste for art/beauty, wealth-accumulation, love of comfort, stubbornness, solid physique.
TAURUS.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Taurus ascendant gives a stout, solid build, a sweet voice, an attractive face, patience, and a love of comfort, art, and stability. Venus’ rulership grants an aesthetic sense, wealth-gathering capacity, and sensual enjoyment; stubbornness and inertia are the flaws. Saravali calls this earth-fixed sign enduring, hard-working, and skilled at accumulation — slow to start but immovable once committed.

VIRGO.ishtaDevata: For Karakamsha in Virgo, the Ishta-devata is Vishnu / Saraswati.
VIRGO.ishtaDevataProse: With the Karakamsha in Virgo, the Ishta-devata is generally Vishnu or Saraswati; worship granting discernment, learning and purity of service is commended.
VIRGO.lagnaPhala: Virgo Lagna: analytical, service-minded, methodical, clean. Mercurial eye for detail (Brihat Jataka 1).
VIRGO.lagnaPhalaGeneral: Analysis, service, cleanliness, fine intellect, methodical skill, over-worry, medium physique.
VIRGO.lagnaPhalaProse: Per Brihat Jataka Ch.1, a Virgo ascendant gives a medium, slender build, a love of cleanliness, analytical skill, a service disposition, humility, and methodical competence. Mercury’s rulership grants a fine intellect, a flaw-detecting eye, and a drive for refinement; over-worry and fault-finding are the flaws. Saravali calls this earth-dual sign hard-working, calculation-skilled, and health-conscious — precise, useful, and discerning.

AADI.phala: Aadi nadi indicates a Vata (air) constitution.
AADI.phalaProse: The Aadi nadi comprises nine nakshatras — Ashwini, Ardra, Punarvasu, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Jyeshtha, Mula, Shatabhisha and Purva Bhadrapada. A person of this nadi has a predominantly Vata constitution: restless, active and quick-thinking. Nadi koota (worth 8 points, the most heavily weighted of the eight kootas) governs health and progeny; partners sharing the same nadi incur the Nadi dosha, which signals risk to offspring and marital harmony. The dosha may be cancelled when both share one nakshatra or differ by pada.

ANTYA.phala: Antya nadi indicates a Kapha (water) constitution.
ANTYA.phalaProse: The Antya nadi comprises nine nakshatras — Krittika, Rohini, Ashlesha, Magha, Swati, Vishakha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana and Revati. A person of this nadi has a predominantly Kapha constitution: steady, calm, enduring and nurturing. In marriage matching, two Antya-nadi partners incur the Nadi dosha, whereas an Aadi-Antya (Vata-Kapha) pairing is considered excellent and conducive to health and progeny.

MADHYA.phala: Madhya nadi indicates a Pitta (fire) constitution.
MADHYA.phalaProse: The Madhya nadi comprises nine nakshatras — Bharani, Mrigashira, Pushya, Purva Phalguni, Chitra, Anuradha, Purva Ashadha, Dhanishtha and Uttara Bhadrapada. A person of this nadi has a predominantly Pitta constitution: sharp, fiery, enthusiastic and inclined to lead. In marriage matching, two Madhya-nadi partners incur the Nadi dosha, signalling risk to health and progeny; the dosha is regarded as most severe in the Madhya nadi.

ANURADHA.namakarana: One born in Anuradha is friendly, cooperative and devoted.
ANURADHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Anuradha (deity Mitra, lord Saturn) is friendly, cooperative, devoted and good at organising. A name reflecting friendship and devotion is commended at the naming.
ANURADHA.phala: Anuradha — a soft nakshatra for friendship, cooperation and auspicious works.
ANURADHA.phalaProse: Anuradha, ruled by Mitra, is a mridu (soft) nakshatra. Friendship, organising and cooperative work, travel and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It grants affection and success and is auspicious.

ARDRA.namakarana: One born in Ardra is sharp-minded, transformative and deep.
ARDRA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Ardra (deity Rudra, lord Rahu) is sharp-minded, transformative, a deep thinker and sensitive. A name reflecting depth and intellect is commended at the naming.
ARDRA.phala: Ardra — a sharp, fierce nakshatra; avoided for auspicious ceremonies.
ARDRA.phalaProse: Ardra, ruled by Rudra, is a tikshna-ugra (sharp and fierce) nakshatra. Vanquishing enemies and sharp, bold deeds are favoured; but it is avoided for marriage, house-beginning and other auspicious rites. Its results are fierce.

ASHLESHA.namakarana: One born in Ashlesha is secretive, shrewd and clever.
ASHLESHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Ashlesha (deity the Serpents, lord Mercury) is secretive, shrewd, clever and fond of mystery. A name reflecting intellect and gravity is commended at the naming.
ASHLESHA.phala: Ashlesha — a sharp nakshatra for mantra and occult work; avoided for ceremonies.
ASHLESHA.phalaProse: Ashlesha, ruled by the Nagas, is a tikshna (sharp, severe) nakshatra. Mantra accomplishment, secret work, poisons/medicine and sharp tasks are favoured; but it is generally avoided for auspicious rites.

ASHWINI.namakarana: One born in Ashwini is swift, radiant and health-giving.
ASHWINI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Ashwini (deity the Ashvini Kumaras, lord Ketu) is swift, radiant, active and inclined to healing. A name reflecting initiative, vigour and a healing aptitude is commended at the naming.
ASHWINI.phala: Ashwini — a nakshatra for swift work, health and travel.
ASHWINI.phalaProse: Ashwini, ruled by the Ashwini Kumaras, is a kshipra (swift, light) nakshatra. Medical treatment, travel, quickly-completed tasks and buying vehicles are favoured. It is health-giving and brisk, but ill-suited to slow, enduring undertakings.

BHARANI.namakarana: One born in Bharani is firm, disciplined and dutiful.
BHARANI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Bharani (deity Yama, lord Venus) is firm of resolve, disciplined, dutiful and just. A name reflecting firmness and purity is commended at the naming.
BHARANI.phala: Bharani — a fierce nakshatra for resolute deeds; avoided for gentle ceremonies.
BHARANI.phalaProse: Bharani, ruled by Yama, is an ugra (fierce) nakshatra. Resolute action, settling disputes and tasks requiring force are favoured; but it is generally avoided for marriage and other gentle auspicious rites.

CHITRA.namakarana: One born in Chitra is beauty-loving, artistic and attractive.
CHITRA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Chitra (deity Tvashtr, lord Mars) is beauty-loving, artistic, attractive and creative. A name reflecting beauty and craft is commended at the naming.
CHITRA.phala: Chitra — a soft nakshatra for art, craft and beauty.
CHITRA.phalaProse: Chitra, ruled by Tvashtr (Vishwakarma), is a mridu (soft) nakshatra. Arts and crafts, decorating the home, clothing and ornaments and works of beauty are favoured. It is attractive and gives gentle results.

DHANISHTHA.namakarana: One born in Dhanishtha is prosperity-loving, rhythmic and generous.
DHANISHTHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Dhanishtha (deity the Vasus, lord Mars) is prosperity-loving, fond of rhythm and music, generous and sociable. A name reflecting prosperity and rhythm is commended at the naming.
DHANISHTHA.phala: Dhanishtha — a movable nakshatra for music, wealth and festivity.
DHANISHTHA.phalaProse: Dhanishtha, ruled by the Vasus, is a chara (movable) nakshatra. Music, financial work, festivity and travel are favoured. It brings prosperity and is mobile, but less suited to fixed work.

HASTA.namakarana: One born in Hasta is skilful, dexterous and industrious.
HASTA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Hasta (deity Savitr, lord the Moon) is skilful with the hands, dexterous, industrious and clever. A name reflecting skill and industry is commended at the naming.
HASTA.phala: Hasta — a swift nakshatra for craft, learning and all auspicious works.
HASTA.phalaProse: Hasta, ruled by Savitr (the Sun), is a kshipra (swift) nakshatra. Handicraft, beginning study, commerce and all auspicious works are favoured. It grants accomplishment and is auspicious.

JYESHTHA.namakarana: One born in Jyeshtha is a leader, a protector and grave.
JYESHTHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Jyeshtha (deity Indra, lord Mercury) is a natural leader, a protector, grave and valuing of experience. A name reflecting leadership and guardianship is commended at the naming.
JYESHTHA.phala: Jyeshtha — a sharp nakshatra for bold deeds and authority; avoided for ceremonies.
JYESHTHA.phalaProse: Jyeshtha, ruled by Indra, is a tikshna (sharp, severe) nakshatra. Bold deeds, taking authority, vanquishing enemies and sharp tasks are favoured; but it is avoided for auspicious rites.

KRITTIKA.namakarana: One born in Krittika is radiant, fearless and a natural leader.
KRITTIKA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Krittika (deity Agni, lord the Sun) is radiant, fearless, a natural leader and sharp of mind. A name reflecting brilliance and leadership is commended at the naming.
KRITTIKA.phala: Krittika — a sharp nakshatra for fire-work, courage and incisive action.
KRITTIKA.phalaProse: Krittika, ruled by Agni, is a tikshna (sharp) and mixed nakshatra. Work involving fire, sharp and courageous deeds, vanquishing enemies and cutting tasks are favoured. It is vitalising but gives fierce results.

MAGHA.namakarana: One born in Magha is dignified, traditional and a leader.
MAGHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Magha (deity the Pitris, lord Ketu) is fond of dignity, traditional, a leader and proud of heritage. A name reflecting honour and tradition is commended at the naming.
MAGHA.phala: Magha — a fierce nakshatra for ancestral rites, authority and tradition.
MAGHA.phalaProse: Magha, ruled by the Pitrs (ancestors), is an ugra (fierce) nakshatra. Ancestral offerings, royal dealings, traditional ceremonies and forceful tasks are favoured; it is less suited to gentle auspicious works.

MRIGASHIRA.namakarana: One born in Mrigashira is curious, gentle and fond of seeking.
MRIGASHIRA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Mrigashira (deity Soma, lord Mars) is curious, gentle, fond of seeking and quick. A name reflecting curiosity and gentleness is commended at the naming.
MRIGASHIRA.phala: Mrigashira — a soft nakshatra for travel, art and gentle works.
MRIGASHIRA.phalaProse: Mrigashira, ruled by Soma (Chandra), is a mridu (soft, tender) nakshatra. Travel, artistic work, music, buying clothes and ornaments and meeting friends are favoured. It gives gentle results and is light in nature.

MULA.namakarana: One born in Mula is investigative, root-seeking and firm.
MULA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Mula (deity Nirriti, lord Ketu) is investigative, given to seeking roots, firm of resolve and a seeker of truth. A name reflecting depth and inquiry is commended at the naming.
MULA.phala: Mula — a sharp nakshatra for uprooting, medicine and incisive work; avoided for ceremonies.
MULA.phalaProse: Mula, ruled by Nirriti, is a tikshna (sharp, severe) nakshatra. Uprooting, medicinal work, mantra practice and incisive tasks are favoured; but it is avoided for marriage and other auspicious rites.

PUNARVASU.namakarana: One born in Punarvasu is optimistic, generous and devout.
PUNARVASU.namakaranaProse: A person born in Punarvasu (deity Aditi, lord Jupiter) is optimistic, generous, devout and able to renew. A name reflecting generosity and dharma is commended at the naming.
PUNARVASU.phala: Punarvasu — a movable nakshatra for travel, renewal and gentle works.
PUNARVASU.phalaProse: Punarvasu, ruled by Aditi, is a chara (movable) nakshatra. Travel, fresh starts, returning home and gentle auspicious works are favoured. It is auspicious and mobile, but yields little for fixed, enduring tasks.

PURVA_ASHADHA.namakarana: One born in Purva Ashadha is invincible-spirited, enthusiastic and influential.
PURVA_ASHADHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Purva Ashadha (deity the Waters, lord Venus) is of an invincible spirit, enthusiastic, influential and firm of opinion. A name reflecting victory and zeal is commended at the naming.
PURVA_ASHADHA.phala: Purva Ashadha — a fierce nakshatra for water-work, victory and bold deeds.
PURVA_ASHADHA.phalaProse: Purva Ashadha, ruled by Apas (the waters), is an ugra nakshatra. Work involving water, victorious journeys, bold deeds and boat-work are favoured. It grants invincibility; it is less suited to gentle ceremonies.

PURVA_BHADRAPADA.namakarana: One born in Purva Bhadrapada is spiritual, grave and intense.
PURVA_BHADRAPADA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Purva Bhadrapada (deity Aja Ekapada, lord Jupiter) is spiritual, grave, intense and philosophical. A name reflecting spirituality and gravity is commended at the naming.
PURVA_BHADRAPADA.phala: Purva Bhadrapada — a fierce nakshatra for intense effort and austerity; avoided for ceremonies.
PURVA_BHADRAPADA.phalaProse: Purva Bhadrapada, ruled by Aja Ekapada, is an ugra (fierce, severe) nakshatra. Austerity, intense practice and forceful deeds are favoured; but it is avoided for marriage and gentle auspicious rites.

PURVA_PHALGUNI.namakarana: One born in Purva Phalguni is genial, generous and fond of art.
PURVA_PHALGUNI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Purva Phalguni (deity Bhaga, lord Venus) is genial, generous, fond of art and of comfort. A name reflecting warmth and artistry is commended at the naming.
PURVA_PHALGUNI.phala: Purva Phalguni — a nakshatra for marriage, love and enjoyment.
PURVA_PHALGUNI.phalaProse: Purva Phalguni, ruled by Bhaga, is an ugra nakshatra. Marriage alliances, affairs of love, arts and pleasure and negotiations are favoured. It brings delight and, despite its fierce class, is suitable for celebration.

PUSHYA.namakarana: One born in Pushya is nurturing, devout and steady.
PUSHYA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Pushya (deity Brihaspati, lord Saturn) is nurturing, devout, steady and service-minded. A name reflecting nourishment and stability is commended at the naming (Pushya is among the most auspicious nakshatras).
PUSHYA.phala: Pushya — the most auspicious nakshatra for all works, except marriage.
PUSHYA.phalaProse: Pushya, ruled by Brihaspati, is a kshipra (swift) and supremely auspicious nakshatra. All auspicious works, accumulating wealth, medicine and coronation are favoured; yet, by classical injunction, it is avoided for marriage.

REVATI.namakarana: One born in Revati is nurturing, compassionate and prosperity-giving.
REVATI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Revati (deity Pushan, lord Mercury) is nurturing, compassionate, prosperity-giving and a guide. A name reflecting nourishment and compassion is commended at the naming (Revati is the auspicious final nakshatra).
REVATI.phala: Revati — a soft nakshatra for travel, nourishment and all auspicious works.
REVATI.phalaProse: Revati, ruled by Pushan, is a mridu (soft) nakshatra. Travel, nurturing work, commerce and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It gives gentle results and protection.

ROHINI.namakarana: One born in Rohini is attractive, creative and fond of prosperity.
ROHINI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Rohini (deity Brahma, lord the Moon) is attractive, creative, fond of art and of prosperity. A name reflecting beauty and creativity is commended at the naming.
ROHINI.phala: Rohini — a highly auspicious fixed nakshatra for stable works, farming and homes.
ROHINI.phalaProse: Rohini, ruled by Brahma, is a dhruva (fixed) nakshatra. Beginning a home, agriculture, buying immovable property, planting trees and all auspicious rites are excellently favoured. It gives stable results and prosperity.

SHATABHISHA.namakarana: One born in Shatabhisha is mystery-seeking, independent and fond of healing.
SHATABHISHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Shatabhisha (deity Varuna, lord Rahu) is mystery-seeking, independent, fond of healing and a deep thinker. A name reflecting insight and independence is commended at the naming.
SHATABHISHA.phala: Shatabhisha — a movable nakshatra for medicine, mantra and secret work.
SHATABHISHA.phalaProse: Shatabhisha, ruled by Varuna, is a chara (movable) nakshatra. Medicinal work, mantra practice, secret tasks and water-work are favoured. It is health-giving but inclined to solitude.

SHRAVANA.namakarana: One born in Shravana is a listener, learning-loving and cultured.
SHRAVANA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Shravana (deity Vishnu, lord the Moon) is a good listener, learning-loving, cultured and skilled in communication. A name reflecting learning and attentiveness is commended at the naming.
SHRAVANA.phala: Shravana — a movable nakshatra for learning, travel and dharma.
SHRAVANA.phalaProse: Shravana, ruled by Vishnu, is a chara (movable) nakshatra. Hearing scripture, study, travel, righteous works and music are favoured. It grants knowledge and is auspicious.

SWATI.namakarana: One born in Swati is independent, balanced and diplomatic.
SWATI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Swati (deity Vayu, lord Rahu) is independent, balanced, diplomatic and mobile. A name reflecting independence and balance is commended at the naming.
SWATI.phala: Swati — a movable nakshatra for trade, travel and independent ventures.
SWATI.phalaProse: Swati, ruled by Vayu, is a chara (movable) nakshatra. Commerce, travel, dealings with vehicles and independent undertakings are favoured. It is mobile and auspicious, but yields little for fixed work.

UTTARA_ASHADHA.namakarana: One born in Uttara Ashadha is righteous, steady and victorious.
UTTARA_ASHADHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Uttara Ashadha (deity the Vishvadevas, lord the Sun) is righteous, steady, victorious and principled. A name reflecting dharma and steadiness is commended at the naming.
UTTARA_ASHADHA.phala: Uttara Ashadha — a fixed nakshatra for lasting victory and dharma.
UTTARA_ASHADHA.phalaProse: Uttara Ashadha, ruled by the Vishvedevas, is a dhruva (fixed) nakshatra. Lasting victory, righteous works, beginning a home and long-term resolves are excellently favoured. It gives stable results and undefeated success.

UTTARA_BHADRAPADA.namakarana: One born in Uttara Bhadrapada is calm, wise and charitable.
UTTARA_BHADRAPADA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Uttara Bhadrapada (deity Ahir Budhnya, lord Saturn) is calm, wise, charitable and grave. A name reflecting calm and wisdom is commended at the naming.
UTTARA_BHADRAPADA.phala: Uttara Bhadrapada — a fixed nakshatra for stable works and depth.
UTTARA_BHADRAPADA.phalaProse: Uttara Bhadrapada, ruled by Ahir Budhnya, is a dhruva (fixed) nakshatra. Stable works, beginning a home, deep resolves and righteous deeds are favoured. It gives stable, calm results.

UTTARA_PHALGUNI.namakarana: One born in Uttara Phalguni is service-minded, trustworthy and steady.
UTTARA_PHALGUNI.namakaranaProse: A person born in Uttara Phalguni (deity Aryaman, lord the Sun) is service-minded, trustworthy, steady and cooperative. A name reflecting trust and service is commended at the naming.
UTTARA_PHALGUNI.phala: Uttara Phalguni — a fixed nakshatra for marriage and enduring works.
UTTARA_PHALGUNI.phalaProse: Uttara Phalguni, ruled by Aryaman, is a dhruva (fixed) nakshatra. Marriage, beginning a home, lasting relationships and long-term works are excellently favoured. It gives stable, auspicious results.

VISHAKHA.namakarana: One born in Vishakha is goal-focused, ambitious and determined.
VISHAKHA.namakaranaProse: A person born in Vishakha (deity Indra-Agni, lord Jupiter) is goal-focused, ambitious, determined and enterprising. A name reflecting purpose and zeal is commended at the naming.
VISHAKHA.phala: Vishakha — a mixed nakshatra for achieving goals and success in contests.
VISHAKHA.phalaProse: Vishakha, ruled by Indra and Agni, is a mishra (mixed, ordinary) nakshatra. Fulfilling resolves, competition, pursuing goals and financial work are favoured; slow at the outset, it grants accomplishment at the end.

GHATI_LAGNA.phala: Ghati Lagna signifies power, administrative authority, status, and rise to high office.
GHATI_LAGNA.phalaProse: The Ghati Lagna is a specialized mathematical ascendant that governs authority, administrative power, fame, and political ascendancy. Advancing at roughly five times the rate of the birth ascendant, it reveals the native’s potential to attain eminent public offices, command others, and receive state honors.

HORA_LAGNA.phala: Hora Lagna is the primary indicator of wealth, financial flows, and material assets.
HORA_LAGNA.phalaProse: The Hora Lagna is a highly specialized mathematical point used to assess financial prosperity, the continuous flow of wealth, and material assets. Its strength, along with the influence of benefic planets upon it, promises financial resilience, generational assets, and success in commerce.

PRANAPADA_LAGNA.phala: Pranapada Lagna signifies constitutional strength, prana, and physical robustness.
PRANAPADA_LAGNA.phalaProse: The Pranapada Lagna is a critical specialized point that governs the life force (prana), constitutional vitality, and physical robustness of the native. Its strength and placement are key in rectifying birth times and determining the longevity, resilience to chronic illnesses, and overall life-force of the body.

SREE_LAGNA.phala: Sree Lagna signifies overall good fortune, Goddess Lakshmi’s grace, and marital abundance.
SREE_LAGNA.phalaProse: The Sree Lagna is a focal point for assessing fortune, the blessing of Goddess Lakshmi, and the qualitative ease of married life. A strongly placed Sree Lagna indicates that marriage will act as a major turning point for financial upliftment, bringing peace, prosperity, and relational bliss.

VARNADA_LAGNA.phala: Varnada Lagna signifies social standing, dharmic role, and public integrity.
VARNADA_LAGNA.phalaProse: The Varnada Lagna is an advanced point used to determine the native's social standing, their authentic professional/dharmic varna, and public integrity. A strong Varnada Lagna secures high respect, moral authority, and acceptance of the native's contributions by the community.

AGNI.phala: Agni (fire) tatwa denotes energy, drive and leadership.
AGNI.phalaProse: The Agni (fire) element comprises seven nakshatras — Magha, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati and Vishakha. A person dominated by it is energetic, enthusiastic, outspoken and endowed with leadership: quick to anger but action-oriented, courageous and fearless, with strong vitality and digestive fire. In elemental compatibility, Fire is friendly with Air (air feeds fire) and opposed to Water.

AKASHA.phala: Akasha (ether) tatwa denotes spirituality, expansiveness and detachment.
AKASHA.phalaProse: The Akasha (ether/space) element comprises five nakshatras — Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada and Revati. A person dominated by it is spiritual, expansive, detached, philosophical and a subtle thinker: broad-minded, freedom-loving and drawn to esoteric knowledge, though sometimes indifferent to practical affairs. As ether is all-pervading and formless, such natives express boundless thought and an orientation toward liberation (moksha).

JALA.phala: Jala (water) tatwa denotes emotion, intuition and nurturing.
JALA.phalaProse: A person dominated by the Jala (water) element is emotional, intuitive, adaptable, nurturing and tender-minded: sensitive, affectionate, retentive of memory and imaginative, able — like water — to take the shape of their circumstances. Its watery quality aligns with the Kapha constitution (the Antya-nadi group), signifying calm, steadiness and nourishment. In elemental compatibility, Water is friendly with Earth and opposed to Fire.

PRITHVI.phala: Prithvi (earth) tatwa denotes stability, patience and practicality.
PRITHVI.phalaProse: The Prithvi (earth) element comprises nine nakshatras — Ashwini, Bharani, Krittika, Rohini, Mrigashira, Ardra, Punarvasu, Pushya and Ashlesha. A person dominated by it is stable, patient, practical, materially grounded, hardworking and dependable: enduring, acquisitive and far-sighted, unshaken even in adversity. In elemental compatibility, Earth is friendly with Water (water makes earth fertile) and mildly opposed to Air.

VAYU.phala: Vayu (air) tatwa denotes intellect, restlessness and communication.
VAYU.phalaProse: The Vayu (air) element comprises six nakshatras — Anuradha, Jyeshtha, Mula, Purva Ashadha, Uttara Ashadha and Shravana. A person dominated by it is intellectual, restless, communicative, changeable and curious: full of fresh ideas, mobile and sociable, though at times mentally unsettled. In elemental compatibility, Air is friendly with Fire and mildly opposed to Earth.

AMAVASYA.phala: Amavasya — the new-moon tithi for ancestral rites; new ventures are avoided.
AMAVASYA.phalaProse: The new-moon tithi, presided over by the Pitrs (ancestors), favours ancestral offerings (tarpana), shraddha, charity and rites of peace; with no Moon visible, new auspicious beginnings are avoided. Good for inner reflection.
