KRISHNA_ASHTAMI.phala: Krishna Ashtami — a Jaya tithi for Shakti worship and fierce undertakings.
KRISHNA_ASHTAMI.phalaProse: The eighth waning tithi, a Jaya tithi presided over by Kala Bhairava, suits worship of Shakti and Kala Bhairava and courageous deeds. It confers strength but with fierce results.

KRISHNA_CHATURDASHI.phala: Krishna Chaturdashi — a Rikta tithi for fierce worship; new ventures are avoided.
KRISHNA_CHATURDASHI.phalaProse: The fourteenth waning tithi, a Rikta tithi presided over by Rudra and Kali, favours Masa Shivaratri, worship of Rudra/Kali and fierce deeds; being Rikta, new auspicious beginnings are avoided.

KRISHNA_CHATURTHI.phala: Krishna Chaturthi — a Rikta tithi for Ganesha worship and clearing obstacles.
KRISHNA_CHATURTHI.phalaProse: The fourth waning tithi, a Rikta tithi presided over by Ganesha, favours Sankashti Ganesha worship and resolves to clear obstacles; being Rikta, new auspicious beginnings are avoided.

KRISHNA_DASHAMI.phala: Krishna Dashami — a Purna tithi for dharma and gentle dealings.
KRISHNA_DASHAMI.phalaProse: The tenth waning tithi, a Purna tithi presided over by Dharmaraja, suits righteous works, gentle dealings and routine auspicious tasks. It is moderately auspicious with calm results.

KRISHNA_DVITIYA.phala: Krishna Dvitiya — a Bhadra tithi for steady work and friendship.
KRISHNA_DVITIYA.phalaProse: The second waning tithi, a Bhadra tithi presided over by Brahma, suits steady work, friendship and gentle dealings. It gives calm results and is moderately auspicious.

KRISHNA_DWADASHI.phala: Krishna Dwadashi — a Bhadra tithi for breaking fasts and charity.
KRISHNA_DWADASHI.phalaProse: The twelfth waning tithi, a Bhadra tithi presided over by Vishnu, suits breaking vows (parana), charity and service to Vishnu. It is gentle and increases merit.

KRISHNA_EKADASHI.phala: Krishna Ekadashi — a Nanda tithi for fasting and devotion to Vishnu.
KRISHNA_EKADASHI.phalaProse: The eleventh waning tithi, a Nanda tithi presided over by Vishnu, favours fasting, worship of Vishnu, vows and righteous works. It grants merit and spiritual accomplishment.

KRISHNA_NAVAMI.phala: Krishna Navami — a Rikta tithi for fierce worship; new ventures are avoided.
KRISHNA_NAVAMI.phalaProse: The ninth waning tithi, a Rikta tithi presided over by Durga, suits worship of the Goddess and fierce deeds; being Rikta, new auspicious beginnings are avoided and caution is advised.

KRISHNA_PANCHAMI.phala: Krishna Panchami — a Purna tithi for wealth matters and medicine.
KRISHNA_PANCHAMI.phalaProse: The fifth waning tithi, a Purna tithi presided over by the Nagas, suits financial dealings, taking medicine and Naga worship. It is moderately auspicious with steady results.

KRISHNA_PRATIPADA.phala: Krishna Pratipada — a Nanda tithi for gentle works and routine beginnings.
KRISHNA_PRATIPADA.phalaProse: The first waning tithi, a Nanda tithi presided over by Agni, suits gentle and routine work; with the Moon waning, ventures meant to grow over time yield less. Moderately auspicious.

KRISHNA_SAPTAMI.phala: Krishna Saptami — a Bhadra tithi for travel and matters of health.
KRISHNA_SAPTAMI.phalaProse: The seventh waning tithi, a Bhadra tithi presided over by the Sun, suits travel, health matters and Sun worship. It is moderately auspicious and vitalising.

KRISHNA_SHASHTHI.phala: Krishna Shashthi — a Nanda tithi for valour and contests.
KRISHNA_SHASHTHI.phalaProse: The sixth waning tithi, a Nanda tithi presided over by Kartikeya, suits acts of valour, contests and work requiring force. It gives enthusiasm and is moderately auspicious.

KRISHNA_TRAYODASHI.phala: Krishna Trayodashi — a Jaya tithi for the Pradosha vow and worship of Shiva.
KRISHNA_TRAYODASHI.phalaProse: The thirteenth waning tithi, a Jaya tithi presided over by Kamadeva and Shiva, favours the Pradosha vow, worship of Shiva and acts of friendship. It grants success and is gentle.

KRISHNA_TRITIYA.phala: Krishna Tritiya — a Jaya tithi for bold action and contests.
KRISHNA_TRITIYA.phalaProse: The third waning tithi, a Jaya tithi presided over by Gauri, suits courageous deeds, contests and resolving disputes. It grants success, though with the fortnight waning its results are milder.

PURNIMA.phala: Purnima — a Purna tithi of the full Moon for all auspicious works and worship.
PURNIMA.phalaProse: The full-moon tithi, presided over by Chandra, carries the full strength of the Moon. All auspicious works, the Satyanarayana vow, charity and ceremonies are favoured. It is supremely auspicious and grants complete results.

SHUKLA_ASHTAMI.phala: Shukla Ashtami — a Jaya tithi for power, worship of Durga and resolute action.
SHUKLA_ASHTAMI.phalaProse: The eighth waxing tithi, a Jaya tithi presided over by Durga, favours worship of Shakti and Durga, courageous deeds and matters involving weapons. It confers victory and strength.

SHUKLA_CHATURDASHI.phala: Shukla Chaturdashi — a Rikta tithi for fierce worship; new ventures are avoided.
SHUKLA_CHATURDASHI.phalaProse: The fourteenth waxing tithi, a Rikta tithi presided over by Rudra (Shiva), favours worship of Rudra and fierce deeds, but being Rikta it is unsuited to new auspicious beginnings.

SHUKLA_CHATURTHI.phala: Shukla Chaturthi — a Rikta tithi for removing obstacles and Ganesha worship.
SHUKLA_CHATURTHI.phalaProse: The fourth waxing tithi, a Rikta tithi presided over by Ganesha, favours worship of Ganesha and the removal of obstacles, but being Rikta it is unsuited to starting new auspicious ventures. Good for resolves to clear hindrances.

SHUKLA_DASHAMI.phala: Shukla Dashami — a Purna tithi for dharma and all auspicious works.
SHUKLA_DASHAMI.phalaProse: The tenth waxing tithi, a Purna tithi presided over by Dharmaraja, favours righteous works, victorious journeys and all auspicious deeds. It is gentle and grants every accomplishment.

SHUKLA_DVITIYA.phala: Shukla Dvitiya — a Bhadra tithi for foundations, friendship and gentle works.
SHUKLA_DVITIYA.phalaProse: The second waxing tithi, a Bhadra tithi presided over by Brahma, favours laying foundations, forming friendships, buying ornaments and gentle auspicious works. It gives steady, calm results.

SHUKLA_DWADASHI.phala: Shukla Dwadashi — a Bhadra tithi for breaking fasts, charity and service to Vishnu.
SHUKLA_DWADASHI.phalaProse: The twelfth waxing tithi, a Bhadra tithi presided over by Vishnu, favours breaking vows (parana), charity, service to Vishnu and auspicious works. It is gentle and increases merit.

SHUKLA_EKADASHI.phala: Shukla Ekadashi — a Nanda tithi for fasting, devotion to Vishnu and dharma.
SHUKLA_EKADASHI.phalaProse: The eleventh waxing tithi, a Nanda tithi presided over by Vishnu, favours fasting, worship of Vishnu, vows and righteous works. It grants spiritual accomplishment and merit.

SHUKLA_NAVAMI.phala: Shukla Navami — a Rikta tithi for fierce deeds; new ventures are avoided.
SHUKLA_NAVAMI.phalaProse: The ninth waxing tithi, a Rikta tithi presided over by Ambika (Durga), favours worship of the Goddess and fierce, courageous deeds, but being Rikta it is unsuited to marriage and other new auspicious beginnings.

SHUKLA_PANCHAMI.phala: Shukla Panchami — a Purna tithi for learning, wealth and medicine.
SHUKLA_PANCHAMI.phalaProse: The fifth waxing tithi, a Purna tithi presided over by the Nagas, favours beginning study, accumulating wealth, taking medicine and worship of Saraswati. It is auspicious and brings prosperity.

SHUKLA_PRATIPADA.phala: Shukla Pratipada — a tithi of new beginnings, growth and auspicious resolve.
SHUKLA_PRATIPADA.phalaProse: The first tithi of the waxing fortnight is a Nanda tithi presided over by Agni. Beginning new ventures, taking resolves, house-entry and auspicious ceremonies are favoured. With the Moon waxing, undertakings that grow are well-supported.

SHUKLA_SAPTAMI.phala: Shukla Saptami — a Bhadra tithi for travel, health and Sun worship.
SHUKLA_SAPTAMI.phalaProse: The seventh waxing tithi, a Bhadra tithi presided over by the Sun, favours travel, matters of health, Sun worship and buying vehicles. It is vitalising and fit for all auspicious works.

SHUKLA_SHASHTHI.phala: Shukla Shashthi — a Nanda tithi for valour, contests and worship of Kartikeya.
SHUKLA_SHASHTHI.phalaProse: The sixth waxing tithi, a Nanda tithi presided over by Kartikeya, favours acts of valour, contests, royal dealings and worship for progeny. It is auspicious and gives enthusiasm.

SHUKLA_TRAYODASHI.phala: Shukla Trayodashi — a Jaya tithi for love, beauty and worship of Shiva.
SHUKLA_TRAYODASHI.phalaProse: The thirteenth waxing tithi, a Jaya tithi presided over by Kamadeva and Shiva, favours affairs of love, enhancing beauty, worship of Shiva and meeting friends. It grants charm and is auspicious.

SHUKLA_TRITIYA.phala: Shukla Tritiya — a Jaya tithi of victory, ceremonies and beginning a home.
SHUKLA_TRITIYA.phalaProse: The third waxing tithi, a Jaya tithi presided over by Gauri, is highly auspicious (as at Akshaya Tritiya). Marriage, beginning construction, buying gold and all auspicious works are favoured; it confers success.

BUDHAVARA.phala: Wednesday, ruled by Mercury — a day of intellect, trade and learning.
BUDHAVARA.phalaProse: Wednesday is Mercury’s day. Intellect, communication, writing, commerce and study are all favoured. Negotiations, accounts and the sending of messages succeed. Mental work prospers by day; study and reflection serve well at night.

GURUVARA.phala: Thursday, ruled by Jupiter — a day of wisdom, dharma and auspicious works.
GURUVARA.phalaProse: Thursday is Jupiter’s day. Wisdom, dharma, service to teachers and auspicious ceremonies are favoured. Teaching, travel, saving wealth and rites such as marriage succeed. Auspicious works bear fruit by day; prayer and study serve well at night.

MANGALAVARA.phala: Tuesday, ruled by Mars — a day of courage, energy and conflict.
MANGALAVARA.phalaProse: Tuesday is Mars’s day. Courage, valour, dealings with land and competitive effort run strong. Clearing debts, contests and bold action succeed — but anger and quarrels must be avoided. Enterprise rewards by day; restraint and calm serve better at night.

RAVIVARA.phala: Sunday, ruled by the Sun — a day of vitality, leadership and health.
RAVIVARA.phalaProse: Sunday is the Sun’s day. It favours self-confidence, leadership, dealings with authority and matters concerning the father. Attending to health, worship and the pursuit of high position are well-supported. The daytime carries bright, active energy; the night is better given to rest and quiet.

SHANIVARA.phala: Saturday, ruled by Saturn — a day of labour, patience and hard tasks.
SHANIVARA.phalaProse: Saturday is Saturn’s day. Labour, patience, service and hard, sustained effort are favoured. Work with iron, fixed assets and long-term undertakings succeed; worship of Hanuman and Saturn is beneficial. Diligence rewards by day; restraint and calm serve at night.

SHUKRAVARA.phala: Friday, ruled by Venus — a day of love, art and enjoyment.
SHUKRAVARA.phalaProse: Friday is Venus’s day. Love, art, music, beauty and pleasure run strong. Matters of marriage, buying ornaments and fine clothing are auspicious. Artistic and pleasurable pursuits bear fruit by day; companionship and delight grace the night.

SOMAVARA.phala: Monday, ruled by the Moon — a day of mind, water and the mother.
SOMAVARA.phalaProse: Monday is the Moon’s day. The mind is gentle and receptive; matters of the mother, water, and the home are favoured, and worship of Shiva is auspicious. Soft, nurturing activities prosper by day; by night the Moon’s strength brings calm and restful sleep.

BRAHMIN.phala: Brahmin varna denotes a knowledge-loving, learned disposition.
BRAHMIN.phalaProse: The Brahmin varna comprises four nakshatras — Krittika, Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha and Purva Bhadrapada. Varna here denotes not social rank but the native’s innate mental orientation; a person of the Brahmin varna is of a sattvic, knowledge-loving, studious and contemplative disposition. Such natives have a natural aptitude for learning, teaching, research, counsel and dharmic pursuits. In Varna koota (worth 1 of the 8 koota points, assessing compatibility of ego and work-orientation) the boy’s varna should be equal to or higher than the girl’s; if it is lower, the varna dosha arises.

KSHATRIYA.phala: Kshatriya varna denotes valor, leadership and authority.
KSHATRIYA.phalaProse: The Kshatriya varna comprises six nakshatras — Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Chitra, Mula, Uttara Ashadha and Uttara Bhadrapada. Varna here denotes the native’s innate mental orientation; a person of the Kshatriya varna is of a rajasic, valorous, leadership-loving and spirited disposition. Such natives have a natural aptitude for command, administration, positions of authority, protection and acts of courage. In Varna koota (worth 1 of the 8 koota points, assessing compatibility of ego and work-orientation) the boy’s varna should be equal to or higher than the girl’s; if it is lower, the varna dosha arises.

MLECCHA.phala: Mleccha falls outside the four classical varnas — unconventional and independent.
MLECCHA.phalaProse: The Mleccha varna comprises seven nakshatras — Bharani, Ardra, Ashlesha, Swati, Vishakha, Shravana and Shatabhisha. The Mleccha is regarded as standing outside the classical four-varna order of Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra, with an innate mental orientation that is independent, unconventional, foreign-leaning and open. Such natives have a natural aptitude for novel work, non-traditional callings, foreign-connected pursuits and self-directed enterprise. Because it lies outside the varna sequence, the ordinary higher-or-lower comparison of Varna koota (worth 1 of the 8 koota points) does not apply to it; it is treated respectfully as standing "outside the classical varna system," not as inferior.

SHUDRA.phala: Shudra varna denotes service, industry and loyalty.
SHUDRA.phalaProse: The Shudra varna comprises five nakshatras — Rohini, Magha, Anuradha, Dhanishtha and Revati. Varna here denotes the native’s innate mental orientation; a person of the Shudra varna is of a service-minded, hardworking, loyal and practically grounded disposition. Such natives have a natural aptitude for service, craftsmanship, skilled manual work, faithful support and labour-intensive callings. In Varna koota (worth 1 of the 8 koota points, assessing compatibility of ego and work-orientation) the boy’s varna should be equal to or higher than the girl’s; if it is lower, the varna dosha arises.

VAISHYA.phala: Vaishya varna denotes trade, practicality and prosperity.
VAISHYA.phalaProse: The Vaishya varna comprises five nakshatras — Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Hasta and Jyeshtha. Varna here denotes the native’s innate mental orientation; a person of the Vaishya varna is of a rajasic yet practical disposition — commercially adept, prosperity-minded and skilled at management. Such natives have a natural aptitude for trade, exchange, finance, agriculture, commerce and enterprise. In Varna koota (worth 1 of the 8 koota points, assessing compatibility of ego and work-orientation) the boy’s varna should be equal to or higher than the girl’s; if it is lower, the varna dosha arises.

ATIGANDA.phala: Atiganda yoga — an inauspicious yoga of obstacles and crisis; new ventures avoided.
ATIGANDA.phalaProse: Atiganda is an inauspicious (severe) yoga indicating crisis and obstruction. New auspicious beginnings are avoided; rites of peace and resolves to clear obstacles are beneficial. Caution is required.

AYUSHMAN.phala: Ayushman yoga — an auspicious yoga for health, longevity and stable works.
AYUSHMAN.phalaProse: Ayushman is an auspicious yoga. Matters of health, enhancing longevity, stable works and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It gives lasting results and promotes well-being.

BRAHMA.phala: Brahma yoga — a highly auspicious yoga for knowledge, creation and all works.
BRAHMA.phalaProse: Brahma is a highly auspicious yoga. Works of knowledge, creative endeavours, beginning a home and all auspicious deeds are excellently favoured. It gives the finest results and is highly auspicious.

DHRITI.phala: Dhriti yoga — an auspicious yoga for patience, steadiness and contentment.
DHRITI.phalaProse: Dhriti is an auspicious yoga. Works requiring patience, steady resolves, contentment and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It confers patience and stable results.

DHRUVA.phala: Dhruva yoga — a yoga of stability, firm resolve and enduring work.
DHRUVA.phalaProse: Dhruva is a “fixed” (sthira) auspicious yoga. Enduring works, beginning construction, buying immovable property and long-term resolves are favoured. It confers firmness and stability, but yields little for fickle, short-lived activity.

GANDA.phala: Ganda yoga — an inauspicious yoga of obstruction; new ventures avoided.
GANDA.phalaProse: Ganda is an inauspicious yoga indicating hindrance and obstruction. New auspicious beginnings are avoided; rites of peace and resolves to clear obstacles are beneficial. Caution is required.

HARSHANA.phala: Harshana yoga — an auspicious yoga for joy, delight and learning.
HARSHANA.phalaProse: Harshana is an auspicious yoga. Joyful activities, festivity, learning and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It brings delight and is auspicious.

INDRA.phala: Indra yoga — an auspicious yoga for prosperity, leadership and authority.
INDRA.phalaProse: Indra is an auspicious yoga. Works of prosperity, leadership, dealings with authority and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It bestows abundance and is auspicious.

PARIGHA.phala: Parigha yoga — an inauspicious yoga of obstruction; new ventures avoided.
PARIGHA.phalaProse: Parigha is an inauspicious yoga indicating barriers and obstruction. New auspicious beginnings are avoided; the latter half carries less fault. Rites of peace are beneficial.

PRITI.phala: Priti yoga — an auspicious yoga for affection, friendship and joy.
PRITI.phalaProse: Priti is an auspicious yoga. Bonds of affection, friendship, joyful pursuits and ceremonies are favoured. It brings love and is fit for all auspicious works.

SADHYA.phala: Sadhya yoga — an auspicious yoga for achievable works and accomplishment.
SADHYA.phalaProse: Sadhya is an auspicious yoga. Accomplishing achievable works, ceremonies and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It helps tasks reach completion and is auspicious.

SAUBHAGYA.phala: Saubhagya yoga — an auspicious yoga for good fortune, prosperity and ceremonies.
SAUBHAGYA.phalaProse: Saubhagya is an auspicious yoga. Marriage, ceremonies, works of prosperity and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It bestows good fortune and is highly auspicious.

SHIVA.phala: Shiva yoga — an auspicious yoga for welfare, dharma and all works.
SHIVA.phalaProse: Shiva is an auspicious yoga. Righteous works, deeds of welfare, worship of Shiva and all auspicious tasks are favoured. It bestows well-being and is highly auspicious.

SHOBHANA.phala: Shobhana yoga — an auspicious yoga for beauty, splendour and ceremonies.
SHOBHANA.phalaProse: Shobhana is an auspicious yoga. Works of beauty, adornment, splendid ceremonies and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It confers radiance and is auspicious.

SHOOLA.phala: Shoola yoga — an inauspicious yoga of conflict and pain; new ventures avoided.
SHOOLA.phalaProse: Shoola is an inauspicious yoga indicating conflict and pain. New auspicious beginnings are avoided; it suits only fierce tasks. Rites of peace are beneficial.

SHUBHA.phala: Shubha yoga — an auspicious yoga for blessings, welfare and all good works.
SHUBHA.phalaProse: Shubha is an auspicious yoga. All auspicious works, fortunate beginnings and deeds of welfare are favoured. It gives auspicious results and is fit for all tasks.

SHUKLA.phala: Shukla yoga — an auspicious yoga for purity, gentle works and ceremonies.
SHUKLA.phalaProse: Shukla is an auspicious yoga. Gentle auspicious works, pure deeds and all auspicious tasks are favoured. It gives gentle results and is auspicious.

SIDDHA.phala: Siddha yoga — an auspicious yoga for accomplishment and all auspicious works.
SIDDHA.phalaProse: Siddha is an auspicious yoga. Accomplishment of all works, auspicious beginnings and study are favoured. It grants success and is auspicious.

SIDDHI.phala: Siddhi yoga — an auspicious yoga for accomplishment and success in all works.
SIDDHI.phalaProse: Siddhi is an auspicious yoga. Beginning ventures, works that grant accomplishment and all auspicious deeds are excellently favoured. It grants success and is highly auspicious.

SUKARMA.phala: Sukarma yoga — an auspicious yoga for good deeds, merit and all works.
SUKARMA.phalaProse: Sukarma is an auspicious yoga. Good deeds, meritorious works, charity and all auspicious tasks are favoured. It grants success in action and is auspicious.

VAIDHRITI.phala: Vaidhriti yoga — a highly inauspicious yoga of great obstruction; all ventures avoided.
VAIDHRITI.phalaProse: Vaidhriti is a highly inauspicious (severe) yoga indicating great calamity. All auspicious beginnings are avoided; only rites of peace, charity and japa are beneficial. Great caution is required.

VAJRA.phala: Vajra yoga — an inauspicious yoga of harshness and impact; new ventures avoided.
VAJRA.phalaProse: Vajra is an inauspicious yoga indicating harshness and sudden impact. New auspicious beginnings are avoided; it suits only fierce, forceful tasks. Caution is advised.

VARIYANA.phala: Variyana yoga — an auspicious yoga for excellent works, comfort and all deeds.
VARIYANA.phalaProse: Variyana is an auspicious yoga. Excellent works, comfort and enjoyment, ceremonies and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It gives superior results and is auspicious.

VISHKAMBHA.phala: Vishkamba yoga — an inauspicious yoga signalling obstacles; caution at the outset.
VISHKAMBHA.phalaProse: Vishkamba is an inauspicious yoga, indicating hindrances at the start. Caution is advised when beginning new auspicious ventures; with effort, success is still possible later. Rites of peace are favoured.

VRIDDHI.phala: Vriddhi yoga — an auspicious yoga for growth, prosperity and wealth.
VRIDDHI.phalaProse: Vriddhi is an auspicious yoga. Increase of wealth, starting business, works of prosperity and all auspicious deeds are favoured. It gives ever-growing results and is auspicious.

VYAGHATA.phala: Vyaghata yoga — an inauspicious yoga of blows and opposition; new ventures avoided.
VYAGHATA.phalaProse: Vyaghata is an inauspicious yoga indicating blows and opposition. New auspicious beginnings are avoided; it suits only fierce tasks. Rites of peace are beneficial.

VYATIPATA.phala: Vyatipata yoga — a highly inauspicious yoga of great obstruction; all ventures avoided.
VYATIPATA.phalaProse: Vyatipata is a highly inauspicious (severe) yoga indicating great calamity. All auspicious beginnings are avoided; only rites of peace, charity and japa are beneficial. Great caution is required.

BUFFALO.phala: Buffalo (Mahisha) yoni denotes strength, endurance and industry.
BUFFALO.phalaProse: The Buffalo (Mahisha) yoni comprises the nakshatras Hasta and Swati. A person of this yoni is strong, enduring, hardworking and firm; serious, slow to anger, accomplishing tasks through toil, and steady. In practical life they bear heavy burdens, are patient, hardy under hardship, and successful in long-term undertakings. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Horse, however, is the Buffalo’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

CAT.phala: Cat (Marjara) yoni denotes an independent, clever nature.
CAT.phalaProse: The Cat (Marjara) yoni comprises the nakshatras Punarvasu and Ashlesha. A person of this yoni is independent, clever, self-willed and watchful; free-spirited, opportunistic, soft on the surface yet protective of self-interest. In practical life they are self-reliant, comfort-loving, subtle in their moves, and careful to guard their own territory. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Rat, however, is the Cat’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

COW.phala: Cow (Go) yoni denotes a gentle, patient and nurturing nature.
COW.phalaProse: The Cow (Go) yoni comprises the nakshatras Uttara Phalguni and Uttara Bhadrapada. A person of this yoni is gentle, patient, nurturing, calm and dharmic; benevolent, generous, industrious and content. In practical life they are devoted to nurturing and care, fond of family, steady of mind, and a benefactor to all through service. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Tiger, however, is the Cow’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

DEER.phala: Deer (Mriga) yoni denotes a gentle, restless and timid nature.
DEER.phalaProse: The Deer (Mriga) yoni comprises the nakshatras Anuradha and Jyeshtha. A person of this yoni is gentle, restless, beauty-loving, timid and sensitive; artistic, easily startled, free-roaming and tender-hearted. In practical life they are delicate, connoisseurs of beauty, averse to confrontation, and fond of peaceful surroundings. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Dog, however, is the Deer’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

DOG.phala: Dog (Shva) yoni denotes loyalty and alertness.
DOG.phalaProse: The Dog (Shva) yoni comprises the nakshatras Ardra and Mula. A person of this yoni is loyal, alert, protective and faithful; courageous, service-minded, devoted to friends and at times quick-tempered. In practical life they are trustworthy, dutiful, guardians of their dependants, and easily won over by affection. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Deer, however, is the Dog’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

ELEPHANT.phala: Elephant (Gaja) yoni denotes dignity, strength and stability.
ELEPHANT.phalaProse: The Elephant (Gaja) yoni comprises the nakshatras Bharani and Revati. A person of this yoni is dignified, strong, steady, patient and commands respect; slow-moving yet resolute, slow to anger and forbearing. In practical life they are magnanimous, capable of carrying great responsibility, and bring stability and prosperity to domestic life. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Lion, however, is the Elephant’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

GOAT.phala: Goat (Mesha) yoni denotes a gentle, mild and affectionate nature.
GOAT.phalaProse: The Goat (Mesha) yoni comprises the nakshatras Krittika and Pushya. A person of this yoni is gentle, mild-natured, affectionate and content; adaptable, sociable, little given to conflict and calm in temper. In practical life they are easily satisfied, warm within family and community, and endeared to all by their soft disposition. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Monkey, however, is the Goat’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

HORSE.phala: Horse (Ashva) yoni denotes a restless, spirited nature.
HORSE.phalaProse: The Horse (Ashva) yoni comprises the nakshatras Ashwini and Shatabhisha. A person of this yoni is restless, spirited, high-energy and enterprising, valuing speed, movement and independence while chafing at stillness. In practical life they are quick to decide, adventurous, well-suited to travel and fieldwork, and intolerant of being controlled. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Buffalo, however, is the Horse’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

LION.phala: Lion (Simha) yoni denotes valor, leadership and dignity.
LION.phalaProse: The Lion (Simha) yoni comprises the nakshatras Dhanishtha and Purva Bhadrapada. A person of this yoni is valorous, a natural leader, dignified, self-respecting and brilliant; fond of their own authority, generous, kind to followers and intolerant of insult. In practical life they are fit for positions of authority, plain-spoken, influential, and independent in decision. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Elephant, however, is the Lion’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

MONGOOSE.phala: Mongoose (Nakula) yoni denotes courage, alertness and agility.
MONGOOSE.phalaProse: The Mongoose (Nakula) yoni comprises the single nakshatra Uttara Ashadha. A person of this yoni is courageous, alert, agile, fearless and resolute; quick to react, skilled in self-defence, composed in crisis and independent. In practical life they remain unshaken in adversity, ready to resist adversaries, firm in resolve, and undeterred by minor fears. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Serpent, however, is the Mongoose’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

MONKEY.phala: Monkey (Vanara) yoni denotes a playful, clever and restless nature.
MONKEY.phalaProse: The Monkey (Vanara) yoni comprises the nakshatras Purva Ashadha and Shravana. A person of this yoni is playful, clever, restless and intelligent; fun-loving, gifted at imitation, versatile and fickle of mind. In practical life they are quick to grasp, sociable, resourceful in their methods, and swift to adapt to new places and tasks. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Goat, however, is the Monkey’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

RAT.phala: Rat (Mushaka) yoni denotes a nimble, resourceful nature.
RAT.phalaProse: The Rat (Mushaka) yoni comprises the nakshatras Magha and Purva Phalguni. A person of this yoni is nimble, clever, acquisitive and intelligent; active, rarely content, engaged in many pursuits and cautious. In practical life they are thrifty, enterprising, quick-witted in crisis, and skilled at gathering resources. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Cat, however, is the Rat’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

SERPENT.phala: Serpent (Sarpa) yoni denotes a secretive, sharp-witted nature.
SERPENT.phalaProse: The Serpent (Sarpa) yoni comprises the nakshatras Rohini and Mrigashira. A person of this yoni is secretive, sharp-witted, perceptive and fond of solitude; inscrutable, retentive of memory, patient for the right moment and at times vindictive. In practical life they are skilled in counsel, calm in crisis, drawn to occult and esoteric knowledge, and slow to reveal their feelings. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Mongoose, however, is the Serpent’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.

TIGER.phala: Tiger (Vyaghra) yoni denotes courage, ferocity and independence.
TIGER.phalaProse: The Tiger (Vyaghra) yoni comprises the nakshatras Chitra and Vishakha. A person of this yoni is courageous, fierce, independent, powerful and proud; fearless, fond of their own authority, capable of acting alone and quick to anger. In practical life they are natural leaders, competitive, intolerant of injustice, and inclined to walk their own path. In Yoni koota — worth 4 of the 8 ashtakoota points, gauging biological compatibility and instinctive temperament — a same-yoni match scores the full 4 and is best; the Cow, however, is the Tiger’s direct enemy yoni, scoring lowest and giving the poorest match.
